No recurrence in the last 400 CI runs (2026-08-19 to 08-24). Duplicate of km-8n62, closed alongside.

title: Re-audit property keys after the promotion-time mint is installed, and one-off register the remainder
description:
Carved out of the slice C bead so it does not close with it. This is an OPERATIONAL check against the live graph, not code work.

Promotion-time schema minting registers a definition on the NEXT promotion of a key, and does no data migration of its own. So a definition-less cell becomes migratable once its key is promoted again — which needs (a) the extension that writes it reinstalled, since the running copy lives in the database rather than in the repo, and (b) that key to actually recur.

WHAT TO DO: after that mint is landed AND installed, run the workspace-wide property audit again. Whatever keys still resolve to nothing have no future promotion coming, and need a one-off registration rather than a design decision.

WHY IT BLOCKS THE FLIP: property migration skips unregistered keys silently, so any key still unregistered at flip time stays cell-only. After a later cell-off cutover a fresh device would have no synced representation of those values at all.

READING THE AUDIT: an empty list means nothing unless the reported sync gap is null — the scan covers materialized local rows only.
close_reason: Re-audited 2026-09-16 with the promotion-time mint installed and running: 8 unregistered keys / 32 cells of 363,981, all dead or owner-gated — five retired names the ledger already records, one more retired kernel name (type) added to RETIRED_PROPERTY_NAMES in this pass, two example-extension gating keys that register when their extension is enabled. No user content is unregistered, so no one-off registration is needed and this does not block the flip. syncGap null on two runs.

title: JSON-family property values shaped like a wikilink mint a phantom alias seat
description:
Sibling of #688, same site, different codec family and a milder failure.

encodedValueToContent's DEFAULT branch (list / refList / raw-json / anything
not string|url|date|number|boolean|ref) writes JSON.stringify(encoded) into the
value child's content verbatim. A nested array serializes to compact JSON that
is itself a whole-block wikilink span:

  JSON.stringify([[1]])      === "[[1]]"
  JSON.stringify([["a"]])    === "[[\"a\"]]"

parseExactReferenceBlockContent reads "[[1]]" as {kind: alias, alias: "1"}, so
core.deriveReferenceTarget stamps reference_target_id and MINTS an alias seat
for a name nothing claims.

Milder than #688 in two ways, which is why it is filed rather than folded into
that fix: no :: marker means is_field_form is never stamped, so the row stays in
the field row value set; and jsonFromContent (JSON.parse) reads "[[1]]" back
correctly. So the value is NOT lost on write. What is wrong is that a JSON value
has become a live reference: a phantom seat exists, and the row is now in reach
of reference maintenance (merge retarget, inline-deleted-block), which rewrites
content — and a rewrite turns the content into invalid JSON, at which point the
value IS lost.

Reachable through the same widening as #688: synthesis picks the raw-json preset
as the catch-all for cell values from importers and raw writers, which nothing
has vetted.

Fix direction, cheaper than the string case because the decode needs no change
at all: when the compact serialization is grammar-shaped, emit indented JSON
(JSON.stringify(v, null, 1)) instead. JSON.parse ignores insignificant
whitespace, so it round-trips as-is, and indented JSON can never take span shape
(a newline always follows an opening bracket, so "[[" and "]]" cannot occur).

Not fixed alongside #688 deliberately: different failure mode, different value
family, and it needs its own test surface. Recorded here rather than as a note
in the #688 PR body.

title: Staging needs_apply over-reports an unchanged re-delivery that arrives while the workspace is deferring
description:
Found by automated review of the materialization-view-gap PR; real, narrow, NOT fixed there — the PR was already six review rounds deep and the last two rounds' findings were regressions from the previous round's fixes, so this was deliberately left rather than edited into the drain's core decision at the end of that session.

WHAT: materializeStagingRows' defer branch records needs_apply = 1 for every row it cannot materialize, exempting only the invisible-either-way case (a staged tombstone whose local row is also absent or tombstoned). It does not exempt the case where the staged row's nonzero updated_at EQUALS the local row's — which invariant I1 (see decideStagingRow) says means identical content, i.e. `blocks` already holds this exact version.

WHY IT MATTERS: getMaterializability can return 'defer' transiently — a key-store read that fails is documented to fail closed that way, not only a locked workspace. An unchanged re-delivery arriving in that window is flagged, its queue entry is consumed by the same drain, and the durable arm of workspaceViewGap then reports a gap with nothing in flight. The reconcile rescan that would re-evaluate it is marker-gated to once per (workspace, client), so an ordinary reopen need not clear it: the workspace can stay refusing every one-way pass (properties migration flip, uploading backfill, orphan-definition mint) until another delivery for that id or an explicit key re-paste.

FIX DIRECTION: "does `blocks` already hold this staged version" is answerable independently of materializability — it is just the equal-nonzero-stamp test. Prefer hoisting it ABOVE the materializability branch so one rule covers both paths, rather than adding a second I1 check inside the defer branch: duplicating decideStagingRow's rule in a second place is the shape the PR's redesign existed to remove.

WATCH FOR: the drain's flag write is the highest-stakes code in that area and the two predicates are disjoint by construction (the queue owns rows the drain has not reached, the flag owns rows it reached and could not apply). Any fix must keep that split, and must not re-flag a row whose queue entry is still pending.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #742); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: Command palette announces the wrong row: aria-activedescendant lags the selection
description:
In the command palette and the block pickers, the input's `aria-activedescendant` points at the PREVIOUSLY selected row after a query change, not the row that is actually selected and highlighted. A screen reader therefore announces the wrong command.

Verified in the live DOM (dev server, 46-row palette, query "bl"): the highlighted row was "New daily block" while `aria-activedescendant` resolved to "Go back in navigation history".

Same root cause as the scroll jump that was just fixed. cmdk's layout-effect queue is flushed with a `Map.forEach`, which visits entries appended DURING the iteration. On a query change, `selectFirstItem` runs inside that flush and calls `setState('value', …)`, which appends two more callbacks — `updateSelectedItemId` and `scrollSelectedIntoView`. Both are then visited by the same in-progress loop, so both read the DOM before React has moved `aria-selected`. Each reads `querySelector('[cmdk-item][aria-selected=true]')` and gets the stale row.

The scroll half was worked around in `CommandList` by redoing the scroll from a microtask. This half cannot be worked around the same way: `selectedItemId` is cmdk-internal state that it renders onto the input and list itself, so an app-level correction would have to write the attribute behind React's back.

Fix direction: correct cmdk's scheduler so the flush does not re-enter — snapshot the queue and swap in a fresh map before iterating, so appended callbacks run in the NEXT commit, after React has re-rendered. Roughly:

    const queued = ref.current
    ref.current = new Map()
    queued.forEach(run)

cmdk is pinned at 1.1.1, which was the latest release as of 2026-08-22 with no upstream fix. So this needs either a pnpm patch (the repo has no `patchedDependencies` yet — this would be the first) or an upstream PR. Worth checking upstream first in case it has since been fixed or reported.

Fixing the scheduler would also make the scroll workaround in `src/components/ui/command.tsx` redundant; it should be removed in the same change rather than left as a second mechanism.

Arrow navigation and pointer hover are NOT affected — they set the value from an event handler rather than from inside the flush.

title: PanelFocusRecovery debounce test red = happy-dom 20.11.0 installed (same cause as the mutationObserverGc failure)
description:
src/plugins/spatial-navigation/test/PanelFocusRecovery.test.tsx > "keeps
extending the debounce while the panel churns, then writes once it settles"
fails with:

  AssertionError: expected "tx" to not be called at all, but actually been
  called 1 times

RESOLVED 2026-08-22 — SAME ROOT CAUSE AS km-ms4t, NOT A SEPARATE FLAKE AND NOT
A TIMING BUG IN THE TEST. The test already drives the debounce with fake
timers, so wall-clock was never involved and no budget needed raising.

PanelFocusRecovery arms its debounced recovery from the panel's
MutationObserver. On happy-dom 20.11.0 that observer's callback is an inline
arrow held only by a WeakRef, so a GC collects it and the observer goes silent.
The churn then delivers no mutations, nothing re-arms the debounce, and the
pending recovery settles mid-churn — which is precisely the early tx the
assertion catches. Fixed on master by d0bf45596 (2026-08-19, happy-dom
->^20.11.2), where the callback is strongly held.

THE FIX IS `pnpm install`.

Measured 2026-08-22, one machine, installed version the only variable:
- 20.11.0, as written:              3/6 runs pass  (the reported ~50%)
- 20.11.0, forced gc() in the churn: 0/6 runs pass  (deterministic)
- 20.11.2, as written:             15/15 runs pass
- 20.11.2, forced gc() in the churn: 10/10 runs pass

Injecting a GC turns the flake deterministic on 20.11.0 and changes nothing on
20.11.2, which isolates GC as the mechanism and the installed version as the
only variable. The gc injection was a probe only and was reverted.

WHY IT PRESENTED AS LOAD-DEPENDENT: agent worktree directories are recycled
across sessions. A new session mints a new branch off current master inside an
existing directory; git refreshes package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml but never
touches the untracked node_modules, which keeps whatever the last install in
that directory produced. So a session can hold a genuinely clean checkout at
current master and a dependency tree days older, with nothing in the failing
output connecting the two. GC timing then decides whether a given run trips.

Before suspecting this test again:
  grep '"version"' node_modules/happy-dom/package.json
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

Full gate on the corrected install: green, 645 files / 8303 tests, 70.7s.
notes: Filed while working on PR https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/735
close_reason:
Not a test bug and not a flake. The test is correct and was doing its job:
detecting that the loaded happy-dom carried the 20.11.0 MutationObserver
regression. Every observed failure came from an environment running 20.11.0
under a checkout asking for ^20.11.2 — already fixed on master by d0bf45596
(2026-08-19). The fix was `pnpm install`; no test was changed.

Root cause of the confusion: agent worktree directories are recycled, so a
session can hold a genuinely clean checkout at current master over a weeks-old
untracked node_modules. A clean checkout is not evidence about the installed
dependency tree.

Recurrence now prevented: `pnpm run check` reconciles the install first
(`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --config.confirm-modules-purge=false`), merged
via PR #741.

title: Alias repair paths stand down on a co-claimed name instead of repairing it
description:
Follow-up from the duplicate-name work (2026-08-21).

getOrCreateDailyNote's repair branch now SKIPS entirely when the row already co-claims any alias with another live block. Reason: the alias trigger deletes and re-inserts the row's whole bag on any properties write, so the duplicate collides and aborts the transaction the repair is riding on — which is the navigation that opened the day. Skipping keeps the day openable; the row stays unrepaired (missing types, wrong parent, missing canonical alias) until the duplicate is resolved.

Two things left open by that choice:

1. getOrCreateKernelPage's repair branch has the SAME whole-bag rewrite and no such guard, so a kernel page that co-claims a name is still un-repairable and takes the caller's tx down with it. Same fix applies; not made there because this work did not touch that path.

2. Nothing surfaces the stood-down state to the user. The duplicate-name banner keys on the page's CONTENT, so a co-claimed name that is not the title shows nothing at all. The page silently stays unrepaired.

Both are downstream of the latent cross-client duplicate wedge, which is the real fix; this is the local mitigation.

title: A materialization-gap refusal names a count but no way to find the rows
description:
Repo.workspaceViewGap refuses a one-way pass when blocks_synced holds rows the device never materialized into blocks, and reports how many. An operator who hits it has no way to see WHICH rows, or why they never materialized, so the only advice the message can give is "reload, or re-enter the workspace key" - which fixes the transient causes and does nothing for the permanent one.

The permanent one is a row whose ciphertext does not decode. materializeStagingRows quarantines it (console.warn, id named) so the drain is not wedged, but nothing durable records it: after a reload the warning is gone and the refusal is indistinguishable from a workspace that merely needs a drain. That workspace can then never run the properties migration, the workspace backfills, or orphan-definition synthesis, and the operator cannot tell why.

Wanted: somewhere to READ the unmaterialized set - ids, workspace, and the reason the last drain declined each (deferred vs quarantined). The agent-runtime health command already reports a materializeBacklog number and is the natural home; the audit-extension / audit-properties verbs are the other candidate. Deciding whether an operator can then OVERRIDE the refusal is a separate question and probably a no.

Follows from the work in the pull request that added workspaceViewGap; the refusal itself is correct and is not what this asks to change.

title: Test suite is blind to timezone bugs: CI runs UTC, so local-time reads pass
description:
A read that should use UTC but uses local time is caught only on a developer machine in a negative-offset zone. Measured on the daily-note date work (2026-08-21): swapping the UTC read of the daily-note date property for a local-time one fails three named tests under TZ=PDT and ZERO under TZ=UTC. GitHub runners default to UTC and no workflow sets TZ, so the gate never sees it.

That inverts where the safety net is: local runs catch these, CI does not. The class is not hypothetical here — the daily-note code deliberately mixes both (dailyNoteDateValue writes midnight UTC for cross-client stability, dailyNoteLocalDate reads local so display labels match the user's calendar day), so getting the direction wrong is an ordinary slip that shifts every date by one day for anyone west of Greenwich.

## Options

- Set TZ to a fixed non-UTC offset for the whole suite (vitest env or the workflow). Cheapest, and makes the offset always non-zero so a local/UTC mix-up cannot cancel out. Risk: tests that silently depend on UTC start failing, which is the point but is a one-time cleanup.
- Run the suite twice at two offsets. Doubles gate time; almost certainly not worth it.
- Pin the specific round-trips (dailyNoteDateValue / dailyNoteIso) in a test that forces its own TZ. Narrow, and does nothing for the next one.

Prefer option 1 unless the cleanup turns out large.

Found while fixing the daily-note identity read; not fixed there because pinning a TZ for the whole suite is its own decision with effects well outside daily notes.

title: Recents navigates to a derived page id that may not exist
description:
Both recents entry points navigate to a derived id that may name no row:

- src/plugins/recents/index.ts - the open_recents action
- src/plugins/recents/HeaderItem.tsx - the header clock button

recentsPageBlockId is a pure uuid-v5 derivation. It names an id; it does not promise a block exists there. With no row, the panel renders blank.

## Reachability, measured (this is the part that was missing)

ensureSystemPages runs at every workspace bootstrap, after the access gate, idempotent and deterministic-id. So the row is present on any normal open. The cases where it is genuinely missing:

1. READ-ONLY / VIEWER WORKSPACE - always missing, unless the owner created it and it synced. This is the most plausible real instance of the bug.
2. The user deleted the page - missing until the next launch, when ensureSystemPages restores it.
3. Bootstrap errored or the access gate has not resolved - but App renders the gate/loader instead of the app tree, so the header is not mounted and the surface is unreachable.

## Why the obvious fix does not work

Resolving through getOrCreateRecentsPage at navigation time does NOT fix case 1: getOrCreateKernelPage has a read-only branch that GETS without creating, so a viewer still lands on nothing. It only fixes case 2, i.e. a deleted page comes back on click instead of at next launch.

It also converts a read-shaped gesture into a source-of-truth write, which drags in every property of the write system. Measured on the attempt: a click silently destroyed the user's pending redo branch (UndoManager.record clears redo on every push, and the create landed alone on the stack); the ensure could run against a workspace other than the active one via an intent-policy retarget; and write eligibility is judged by a repo-wide flag while the write names a workspace (see the separate root bead). Four review rounds, all the same root.

## The direction worth trying instead

The Recents page row holds no content. RecentsPageBlockRenderer.canRender dispatches on the block's stored types containing RECENTS_PAGE_TYPE, and the feed itself comes from the recentActivity workspace query - it never reads the page's children. So the row is a type tag plus a navigation anchor.

If the renderer matched on IDENTITY instead - block.id === recentsPageBlockId(block.workspaceId) - a navigation to a nonexistent derived id would render the feed anyway, viewers included, with no write on any gesture. That fixes case 1 and case 2 together and removes the whole mutation-on-click class.

NOT YET VERIFIED, check before committing to it: whether a Block handle for a nonexistent row carries a usable workspaceId, and how the panel renders a block that does not exist. If the renderer plumbing needs the row after all, this direction collapses.

## Prior attempts, both abandoned

- PR 468 (branch claude/kernel-page-raw-id-callers): assumed an alias-first adoption design that was rejected.
- PR 720 (branch claude/beautiful-mirzakhani-b90133): added an ensureTarget option to navigation. Closed unmerged after the reachability analysis above showed it fixes only case 2. The branch is kept - two pieces there are worth salvaging independently of the approach: threading skipUndo through getOrCreateKernelPage so a machinery write stays out of undo history, and the reasoning about narrowing a get-or-create to the caller's own workspace.

title: Property-definition projector fence flakes in CI: a delete is occasionally never observed
description:
The test 'skips a key whose definition the user deleted, rather than resurrecting it' in propertyDefinitionSynthesis.test.ts failed once in CI with 'expected resolved not to be resolved' — its untilKeyUnresolved fence timed out after 10s with the resolver still reporting the pre-delete state.

Evidence gathered:
- Measured the real mechanism: delete -> resolver reports unresolved takes 28ms, five runs, no variance. The fence budget is 10,000ms, a 357x margin. Per the repo's own timeout guidance (p99.9 wall-clock stretch under gate load is ~6x) a budget increase is NOT the fix and would be papering over.
- Could not reproduce: 12 isolated runs of the file and 6 runs of the enclosing directories at CI's worker count, all green.
- Re-running the identical CI job on the same commit passed.
- The fence has been in the file for 44 commits with 8+ green CI runs before this, so it is a low-rate pre-existing flake rather than a regression.

Reading per the project's testing doctrine: a wait that fails with the value still at its STARTING state after 357x the measured latency is a DEAD mechanism in that run, not a slow one — i.e. the projector's change notification was missed, not late. That is either a real (rare) gap in projector notification for soft-deletes, or a test-harness race around the shared test database.

Why it is not fixed inline: there is no catch-up flush to await. whenPropertyDefinitionsReady awaits only the initial prime, not catch-up, so every test that needs the projection to have observed a write polls for it. A deterministic fix wants a test-only 'projectors have settled' affordance, which is its own piece of work.

Do NOT fix this by raising the fence budget.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #714); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: Properties migration: two devices can publish divergent synthesized definitions before the backfill claim
description:
The one-time properties migration acquires its graph-wide claim inside the backfill runner, which is AFTER synthesis has already committed definition blocks.

Two devices that both pass the confirmation dialog before either writes can therefore publish definitions for the same orphan key with different presets. Deterministic ids mean they write the same block rather than two rivals, so last-writer-wins picks one — but the preset each device chose is a local decision (an extension that replaces a value preset is dropped from that device's ladder, so one device can prove 'string' where another falls through). The backfill claim then decides only which device WRITES the children; if sync later settles on the other device's definition metadata, migrated children decode under a codec the definition does not declare.

Mitigations already in place: the confirmation dialog says explicitly to run it in one place, and the second device converges on an existing definition rather than overwriting it once the first has landed — so the window is genuine simultaneity plus a divergent preset override.

Fix direction: acquire the graph-wide claim before synthesis and hold it through the flip and backfill, rather than taking it inside the backfill runner. That is a restructuring of the claim lifecycle, which is why it was not done inline during review.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #710); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: A defineProperty owner is invisible to name resolution, so synthesis claims its key
description:
`defineProperty` produces a bare `PropertySchema` with no definition block and
no seed. `SnapshotPropertySchemaResolver.resolveName` sees definition blocks and
seeds only — a plain schema is reachable only through `resolveBoundary(handle)`,
and `allowUnregisteredPlainSchemas` is what lets its writes land for the active
workspace.

So a key owned by an ENABLED extension through `defineProperty` is
indistinguishable, to every name-based consumer, from a key nobody owns:

- `audit-properties` reports it as unregistered
- orphan synthesis (#679) treats it as a candidate and mints a user-origin
  definition claiming the name
- the owner's subsequent writes then fail `shadowed`, because `resolveBoundary`
  finds a winner that is not the caller's schema

This makes the migration runbook's advice WRONG for that class. The module
header, `audit-properties`' `undeclaredFix` and the migration confirmation
dialog all say "install or enable the owner first, then synthesize" — which
works for a SEED owner (enabling materializes its definition, so the key stops
being orphaned) and does nothing at all for a plain-schema owner. Enabling the
extension changes nothing that name resolution can see.

Not fixable from the consumer side: there is no registry of active plain-schema
owners to inventory. That is what makes them plain.

Options, none of them synthesis's to pick:
- make plain schemas visible to name resolution (a registry of live handles),
  so `resolveName` can report the key as owned
- have `defineProperty` mint a definition block on first use, which is what
  every other owner does
- declare `defineProperty` unsuitable for keys that must survive the properties
  migration, and say so where it is documented in the extension API catalog

Found in review of PR #686. The wording in those three places has been corrected
to stop promising the ordering fixes it, but the underlying gap remains.

title: Nightly fuzz failure (2026-08-21)
description:
Nightly fuzz run failed: https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/actions/runs/32457501073 (full logs in the run's fuzz-output artifact).

- `src/plugins/references/test/referencesRecompute.fuzz.test.ts`

**Triage:** the deep tier runs green by default — there is no known standing red, so every file listed above is a real signal until shown otherwise. It is one of two things:
1. **A product bug** — the property caught something real. Reproduce with the commands at the bottom, then fix the code.
2. **An unsound oracle** — the property asserts something the code never promised, or the counterexample doesn't survive replay (see the shrink-unsoundness note below). Fix the property.
