That's the existing override mechanism — plugins replace kernel registrations by registering after them. It works, but the warn is easy to miss and accidental name collisions silently overwrite intended behavior.

## Current state (verified)

All ~8 facets in `src/data/facets.ts` use an identical combine: build a `Map<string, …>`, `console.warn` on duplicate, `set` (last-wins). No `overrides` field, no throw-on-collision.

## Fix shape

Registrations may opt into a checked override target:

```ts
propertySchemasFacet.of(statusPropV2, {source: 'my-plugin', overrides: 'status'})
```

`combine` asserts an entry under `overrides` exists; if absent, **throw** (catches typos). If present, replace silently (intent declared, no warn). Without `overrides`, any duplicate-name collision **throws** (catches accidents). Strict mode + intentional override + typo catch in one shape. ~10 lines per facet's combine; apply uniformly.

**Trigger to build:** plugin authors stepping on each other's schema/mutator/processor names in the wild and warn-and-last-wins not catching it in review. Until then the existing convention works for the alpha-stage plugin surface.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Drop unflushed ps_crud for local-only mode (and reduce import bloat)
description:
## Problem

`ps_crud` is PowerSync's outgoing upload queue. The Roam import (run with `source='user'`) enqueued 304k rows ≈ 204 MB. In `localOnly` mode (no remote sync) those entries can never drain; with remote sync on but a massive import, the queue still bloats local storage until it drains.

## Current state (verified)

- `TxSource` is only `'user'` (`src/data/api/changeScope.ts`); all `ChangeScope` entries map to `source='user'`.
- Roam import uses default `repo.tx(...)` (source `'user'`) — `src/plugins/roam-import/import.ts`.
- No `discardPendingUploads` action exists.

## Two angles

- **Cleanup option** — when `localOnly` is active, expose a `discardPendingUploads()` action that truncates `ps_crud` (or raw `DELETE FROM ps_crud`, since nothing reads it locally). Frees ~200 MB on this DB.
- **Don't enqueue during import** — the upload trigger gates on `tx_context.source = 'user'`. Add a fourth source value `'import'`; both the upload trigger and `row_events` trigger learn to ignore it; the Roam import wraps its txs with `source: 'import'`. Then both `ps_crud` AND `row_events` stay small even on bulk import (the latter trims an additional ~250 MB of audit bloat — overlaps with the row_events-trim issue).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Periodic row_events trim (bound the per-row audit log)
description:
## Problem

`row_events` is the per-row audit + invalidation log. It is trigger-written and **never trimmed** — it grew to 262 MB / 304k rows on the import-heavy DB. The fast path doesn't need history; the row_events tail consumes by ascending `id` and only needs rows newer than its high-watermark. Long-tail entries are dead weight on disk and on backup/export.

## Current state (verified)

- `row_events` defined in `src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts` with AUTOINCREMENT id, no trim logic.
- No `DELETE FROM row_events` anywhere; only `MAX(id)` reads for watermark tracking (`rowEventsTail.ts`).

## Fix shape

At startup (or on a low-priority idle hook), `DELETE FROM row_events WHERE id < (MAX(id) - K)` for some K (e.g. 50 000), or `WHERE created_at < ?` with a 7-day window. Either runs in one statement; the index on `id` is the auto PK. Optional: bound `command_events` with the same shape (small today, same unbounded shape).

Note: PowerSync's CRUD-apply path writes a row_event per sync write, so even a fully-synced read-only client accumulates. Worth doing.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Reduce per-block flicker on lazy hierarchical loads — wrap expand toggles in useTransition
description:
## Problem

`useChildIds` is backed by `repo.childIds`, which hydrates the whole children list per parent on first read. That keeps the per-parent expand path fast, but as the user scrolls into deeper levels their grandchildren still load on `LazyBlockComponent` mount and visibly pop in.

## Current state (verified) — most of this is already done

- ✅ **Structural skeleton**: `src/components/BlockLoadingPlaceholder.tsx` already renders a `BulletDot` at the right indent inside a block-shaped flex layout (not a bare 32px `<div>`).
- ✅ **Overscan**: `OVERSCAN_PX = 600` in `src/components/LazyBlockComponent.tsx`.
- ✅ **`repo.childIds`** id-only query (`core.childIds`) backs `useChildIds`.
- ❌ **`useTransition` around expand toggles** — NOT done. `DefaultBlockRenderer` calls `await setIsCollapsed(!isCollapsed)` directly with no `startTransition`.

## Remaining work

`startTransition`-wrap the `setIsCollapsed` write so React keeps showing the previous tree until the new descendant Suspense boundaries resolve, instead of flashing fallbacks during the load window. (`src/components/renderer/DefaultBlockRenderer.tsx`.)

Optional, if it still feels jumpy after that: tighter overscan / prefetch — warm a few levels of `repo.childIds` ahead of intersection.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2). Scope reduced: skeleton + overscan already shipped; only the `useTransition` piece remains._

title: Move properties_json / references_json to JSONB across the data layer
description:
## Problem

`properties_json` and `references_json` are stored as `text` everywhere — Postgres column, PowerSync sync stream, local SQLite. There are ~29 `json_extract` / `json_each` callsites over these columns (including per-write triggers in `src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts` on `$.alias` and `$.types`) that re-parse the whole text blob on every call. JSONB would walk the binary structure directly — bigger blobs and hotter paths get the bigger win.

## Current state (verified)

- `src/data/blockSchema.ts`: `properties_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`, `references_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` (Postgres + local SQLite).
- `blockToRowParams` still does `JSON.stringify(...)` for both.
- Read path wraps in `json(properties_json)` / `json(references_json)`.

Out of scope for the per-key `properties_json` merge work (`docs/field-level-sync-merge.md`): the correctness fix doesn't need it, and the migration has a real rollout-compat problem worth handling in isolation (old clients send `JSON.stringify(properties)` strings; a string body in a `jsonb` column stores a JSONB *string scalar*, not the object).

## Fix shape (when triggered)

- Bundle the Postgres column migration with the client uploader change that sends objects/arrays instead of strings.
- Defensive server-side normalization for inflight stringified writes during rollout: `CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(properties_json) = 'string' THEN properties_json #>> '{}' ELSE properties_json END`.
- Re-create `idx_blocks_workspace_with_references` with the jsonb predicate (`references_json <> '[]'::jsonb`).
- Local side: confirm wa-sqlite supports SQLite 3.45+ JSONB; wrap each `SELECT properties_json` in `json(properties_json)` so the JS driver still gets text; change pull-down `put` SQL to `jsonb(?)`; verify the shape of `CrudEntry.previousValues.properties_json`.
- **Benchmark** on a representative block count (import-heavy DB) before committing — the win has to be measured.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Schema-rename does not cascade — instance values orphan on rename
description:
## Problem

When a user renames a `property-schema` block (editing `property-schema:name` via `PropertySchemaBlockRenderer`), the schema republishes under the new name but every instance block's `properties_json` is still keyed by the **OLD** name. The old name has values but no schema; the new name has a schema but no values. **The renamed property silently disappears from the UI** (and its data is effectively orphaned).

## Current state (verified)

- `PropertySchemaBlockRenderer.writeName` only calls `block.set(propertyNameProp, next)` — it updates the schema block's name and nothing else.
- `properties_json` is keyed by `schema.name` (`src/data/block.ts` reads `data.properties[schema.name]`).
- No cascade-rename, no block-id keying.

## Two viable fixes

- **Cascade-rename**: on schema name change, walk every block where `properties_json` has the old key and rewrite the key to the new name in one tx. Surgical; no data-model change. Cost: high-fanout schemas (e.g. renaming `status` across 50K blocks) rewrite a lot of rows under PowerSync's serialized writer; mid-rename conflict resolution must handle blocks transiently carrying both keys.
- **Block-id keying** (see companion issue): `properties_json` keys become schema block-ids. Renames become free at the value layer. Requires resolving "what's the block-id for a kernel/plugin schema?" and a one-time migration of every existing `properties_json` blob.

User is leaning toward **block-id keying as the destination** (composes with the "id-stable handle" decision for types). Cascade-rename remains a viable interim step that doesn't paint into a corner.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2). Companion to the block-id-keying issue._

title: CI guard on Postgres ↔ TS schema drift
description:
## Problem

`scripts/gen-sync-config.ts` keeps the local-SQLite raw-table mapping and the PowerSync sync-stream SELECT in lockstep (both projected from `BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS` / `WORKSPACE_*` arrays), and `check:sync-config` enforces TS ↔ PowerSync consistency in CI. **But Postgres is still drift-prone** — someone can edit `BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS` without writing the matching `supabase/migrations/<…>.sql`, and nothing fails until `db push` (or worse, a runtime PATCH referencing a missing column).

## Current state (verified)

- `check:sync-config` runs via `yarn run check` (`scripts/check.mjs`, `.github/workflows/run-tests.yml`) — validates TS ↔ PowerSync only.
- `BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS` lives in `src/data/blockSchema.ts`.
- **No** Postgres-drift CI step, **no** `yarn snapshot:schema` script, **no** `supabase/schema-snapshot.json`.

## Fix shape

A CI step that asserts the Postgres column set is a **superset** of every name in the TS column lists. Options:

- Query the linked DB: `npx supabase db query --linked "SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name IN ('blocks','workspaces','workspace_members')"` and diff against the TS arrays. Cost: needs a Supabase-reachable env in CI.
- Or a checked-in `supabase/schema-snapshot.json` regenerated via `yarn snapshot:schema` and diffed (no live DB).
- Lower-effort variant: parse migration files as text and grep for `add column.*<name>` per TS column — no DB connection, but misses dropped columns.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P1). Note: partial mitigation (`check:sync-config`) already exists; this covers the Postgres gap specifically._

title: Action/context resolution: filters can only opt in (OR), so modal contexts can't yield to text editing
description:
## Problem

The reconciler decides whether to handle a key event by **OR-ing** the `eventFilter` of every active context:

```ts
// src/shortcuts/HotkeyReconciler.tsx:90
for (const type of active.keys()) {
  if (config?.eventFilter?.(event)) return true   // any filter can opt IN
}
return defaultEventFilter(event)
```

Because composition is OR-only, an `eventFilter` can **only widen** the set of handled events — it can never veto. Concretely, `EDIT_MODE_CM`'s filter returns `true` for events inside `.cm-editor` (`src/shortcuts/defaultContexts.ts:48`), opting editor events *back into* dispatch. When a modal context is active at the same time (e.g. SRS review's reveal/grade context over a revealed-answer CodeMirror), it shadows edit-mode and eats keys like Enter / 1‑4 while the user is typing. There's no way for the modal context to declaratively say "I yield while focus is in an editor."

The current workaround (PR #63, `src/plugins/srs-review/ReviewSession.tsx`) gates at *activation*: deactivate the whole context when focus lands on an editable element (`isEditableElement`). This works but:
- pushes focus→activation plumbing into each feature component;
- re-implements editable-target detection that already exists (`isEditorElement` / `shouldExitEditModeAfterBlur`, `src/utils/dom.ts:37`);
- will be copy-pasted by every future modal context.

## Direction (general, not a single point-fix)

Rather than only adding a `suppressInEditableTarget` flag, rework how the reconciler **resolves which active context wins an event** so that suppression/veto is expressible centrally. Things to weigh:

1. **Tri-state filters** — `handle` / `ignore` / `veto`, so a context can actively suppress lower-priority contexts instead of only opting in.
2. **Precedence-based single-winner resolution** — modal/exclusive contexts declare higher precedence; the reconciler picks one winning context per event rather than OR-ing all filters.
3. **Declarative editable-target awareness** — e.g. `suppressInEditableTarget` / `modal` flags evaluated centrally against the shared `isEditorElement` helper, so features stop hand-rolling focus gating. (This is the cheap subset of the above and could ship first to retire the PR #63 workaround.)

## Acceptance
- A modal context can declaratively yield to text editing (no per-component focus gating).
- Editable-target detection lives in one place (reuse `src/utils/dom.ts`).
- Document the new resolution/precedence semantics; existing single-context behavior preserved.
- As a follow-up, delete the `surfaceFocused` / `isEditableElement` workaround in `ReviewSession.tsx`.

Context: surfaced during PR #63 (spaced-repetition review UI).

title: appMountsFacet (and id-bearing facets) should dedup by logical `id`, not just FacetContribution reference
description:
## Problem

The resolver dedups contributions by **`FacetContribution` object identity**:

```ts
// src/extensions/resolveAppRuntime.ts:158
if (seen.has(node)) return
seen.add(node)
```

This is the right granularity for **reference-stable, idempotent** contributions — e.g. exported singleton data/schema extensions like `dailyNotesDataExtension`. Every plugin that bundles the same exported object hits `seen.has(node)` and it registers exactly once.

It is the **wrong** granularity for app mounts. `appMountsFacet` uses the default combine, which keeps every value:

```ts
// src/extensions/facet.ts:83
combine: combine ?? (values => values as unknown as Output)   // keeps all
```

and mounts are contributed *inside plugin factories*, so each call mints a fresh `FacetContribution`:

```ts
// src/plugins/daily-notes/index.ts:196
appMountsFacet.of(reschedulePickerMount, {source: 'daily-notes'}),
```

`AppMountContribution` carries an `id` (e.g. `'daily-notes.reschedule-picker'`) that *looks* like an identity key, but the combine ignores it — it's only metadata. So if two code paths each contribute the same logical mount (e.g. daily-notes and some plugin that wants to "bundle" the picker), reference dedup never fires and **both render**. For the reschedule picker that means two `<ReschedulePicker/>`, two `window.addEventListener(openReschedulePickerEvent, …)` (`src/plugins/daily-notes/ReschedulePicker.tsx:168`), and a single dispatch handled twice.

This is the trap that made bundling the picker mount unsafe in the SRS-review work (PR #63) — we had to gate / treat daily-notes as a hard dep instead of re-contributing the mount.

## Proposal

Give `appMountsFacet` (and any other facet whose values carry a logical `id`) an **id-keyed combine** that collapses duplicates by `id` — last-wins or first-wins, whichever we standardize — so a logically-singleton mount stays single no matter how many plugins reference it.

Options to consider:
- An id-dedup combine specifically on `appMountsFacet`.
- A small reusable `dedupById` combine helper for any id-bearing facet.
- A dev-mode warning when two surviving contributions share an `id` (catches accidental double-mounts even where last-wins is "fine").

## Acceptance
- Two contributions of the same mount `id` result in a single mount.
- Existing single-contribution behavior unchanged.
- Decide + document the tie-break (precedence/order) for same-`id` collisions.

Context: surfaced during PR #63 (spaced-repetition review UI).

title: Reference readers disagree on content that is exactly [[a]]]
description:
The two reference readers disagree on content that is exactly `[[a]]]`. The whole-block reader `parseExactReferenceBlockContent` (src/data/referenceBlock.ts) reads it as a reference block to alias `a]`; the inline reader (`parseReferences`, src/plugins/references/referenceParser.ts) reads `[[a]]` followed by a stray `]`. The module header says the readers must not drift, and this divergence is not among the ones it lists as deliberate.

Since 2026-11-05 a label/property/tag name ending in an unmatched `]` is refused at write time (`endsInUnmatchedBracket`), so new content of this shape is not minted by the app, but hand-typed or imported content can still hold it.

Fix direction: make the whole-block reader follow the inline one (reject an alias whose raw text ends in an unmatched `]`). Decision needed because that changes the derived reference target of existing rows with such content on their next derive (derived state, not source text; size it first with one read-only query over blocks whose content matches the shape).

title: Evaluate vitest isolate:false (~118s estimated on a ~356s test task)
description:
Evaluate running vitest with `isolate: false`.

Measured on a 4-CPU cloud container (2026-11-05): the full test task takes ~356s, and vitest reports import at 38% of tracked time, estimating "~117.65s faster with isolate: false — shared modules are evaluated once per worker instead of once per file". The per-file speedups in the 2026-11 test audit barely moved the gate's wall clock (361s -> 356s) because import dominates.

Risk: test files would share module state per worker (module-level singletons, registries, process-global latches such as the edit-mode keepalive, `vi.mock` hoisting, happy-dom globals). Approach: try it on a branch, run the suite several times with `--sequence.shuffle`, list the files that fail only when sharing a worker, and decide between fixing those leaks or opting just those files back into isolation (a separate vitest project).

title: Caret lands at column 0 when arrowing out of a block about 130-140ms after typing
description:
## Observed (2026-11-04)

Production build, local-only workspace, headed Chromium driven by Playwright with real key events. Type three characters, wait the given gap, press ArrowDown, read the caret column in the block it lands on. The correct column was 25. Trials that landed at column 0, out of 15 per cell:

| Gap | 1x CPU, helper off | 1x CPU, helper on | 4x CPU, helper off | 4x CPU, helper on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 120ms | 1 | 2 | 7 | 5 |
| 130ms | 9 | 10 | 11 | 11 |
| 140ms | 10 | 12 | 13 | 10 |
| 150ms | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

"Helper" is the flush added by the focus-ordering PR for this editor. It makes no clear difference (51 of 120 off, 50 of 120 on), so this predates that change. The text is never affected.

## Reasoned, not measured

`pushSelection` in `src/components/BlockEditor.tsx` is debounced by 150ms. Its guard skips the write once focus has moved. A navigation writes the target block's `editorSelection` and then moves focus in a second transaction. If the timer fires between the two, the guard still passes and the stale selection overwrites the target's, so the new editor doesn't place the caret.

## Fix direction

Write the selection and the focus move in one transaction, for example a `selection` option on `focusBlock`, which has about 10 callers, and re-check focus inside `pushSelection`'s own transaction, as `exitEditModeForBlock` does. Both are needed: a timer firing while the navigation's transaction is in flight still passes a guard that reads the cache.

title: Decide whether and when to adopt a native app shell across platforms
description:
## Summary

Decide whether, and when, Knowledge Medium should run inside a native app shell on desktop and mobile. This is deliberately not a commitment to build one: earlier ideas never had a concrete "we need this" case, so the first job is to name the trigger.

The vision worth evaluating: the same hosted web app on every platform, with the shell adding capabilities and no native UI. Every feature keeps working in a plain browser, so most changes still ship on the normal web deploy cycle.

Everything below is from research and reasoning in November 2026. Nothing has been prototyped.

## Candidate use cases

| Candidate | Would a shell fix it? | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Independent per-device client for a third-party messenger (WhatsApp as the worked example) | Yes, and iOS appears to need native code | Clearest case, if that client is built |
| iOS local database corruption (#284) | Possibly, with native SQLite | Strong if it recurs with data at risk |
| Multi-tab OPFS write stalls (#255, no longer open) | Yes, on desktop | Re-check before counting it |
| Receiving the iOS share sheet | Probably; recalled, not checked | Nice to have |
| Keeping a live app tab for the agent bridge | Yes, but one machine can do this without a shell | Not sufficient alone |
| iOS keyboard bugs | No; Capacitor on iOS is still WebKit | Does not count |

## Platform constraints

- **Fast updates only cover the web layer.** Native capabilities ship on each platform's own cycle, and iOS is the slowest. Hosted code will run against older shells, so every capability needs feature detection.
- **Desktop:** Electron can load the hosted app and gives the same engine on every OS, plus Node. Tauri uses WebKit on macOS. Electron's security guide says to validate IPC senders against an origin allowlist.
- **PR previews share production's origin**, so an origin check cannot tell them apart. A shell must also pin navigation and IPC to the production path, or serve the app from its own origin.
- **iOS:** Capacitor documents `server.url` as not intended for production, and a shell that only loads a website risks App Store rejection (guidelines 4.2 and 2.5.2, per third-party checklists). Likely shape: bundled assets plus live updates, which apply on the next restart.
- **Native storage is the expensive part.** A browser fallback keeps OPFS, so there would be two storage backends. The PowerSync Capacitor SDK uses native SQLite and is in beta per its docs. The data layer already runs on `@powersync/node` in tests.
- **A shell is a new device.** It gets its own storage, so expect a full resync. E2EE keys live in IndexedDB and do not carry over, so a migration must confirm the workspace key is available first and leave the existing browser install untouched.
- **Extensions have no capability boundary.** Imports are not gated; the only gate is per-device approval to run. Any approved extension could use anything the shell exposes to the page, so sensitive operations need limits in the native layer.

## Learnings from Beeper

From Beeper's own 2024-2025 posts and docs, so details may have changed.

- It moved bridges from its cloud into each app, citing end-to-end encryption and conflict with networks.
- Each device connects to each network separately. Only chat state such as pins and archive syncs between devices.
- iOS uses a native Notification Service Extension with tight memory limits. Its backend registers for the networks' pushes and forwards encrypted payloads, so "on-device" still needs a small push relay.
- A shared SDK leaves UI and storage to each app.
- Its local Android Signal bridge cut those chats off from Matrix bots, so independence can cost integrations.
- It warns that it is not a history backup.
- Its Desktop API offers local access to chats, including sending, but only while the desktop app runs and by default only on that device.

## Lessons for a messaging client

- Clients connect directly and keep their own keys. KM sync carries only the layer on top, never Signal keys.
- Messages can still be blocks: the Matrix extension's deterministic ids let several devices ingest one event, with the first write winning. Edits and reactions need more than that, and derived ids must use the keyed namespace (`deriveWorkspaceIdNamespace`), since ids sync in plaintext.
- Inbound text must never be parsed as references. Otherwise a received `[[claude]]` could create the backlink that starts an agent-dispatch run. Reasoned from the watcher design, not tested.
- A web-only client is unlikely to work. Old reverse-engineering notes say WhatsApp rejects connections without its own Origin header, which page scripts cannot set. iOS PWAs also lack background work and silent push.
- Unofficial WhatsApp clients conflict with its terms and carry account-ban risk, in any architecture. No reliable ban rates were found.

## Cheaper test before any shell

Build a KM extension on Beeper's Desktop API to learn whether malleable chat inside KM is worth having, with no protocol client, key handling or shell. Still unchecked: whether a hosted tab can reach its local port, whether new messages can be streamed, and the current encryption status of its on-device connections.

## Acceptance criteria

- A named trigger for adopting a shell, or a recorded decision not to, with the reason.
- If adopting: a per-platform plan covering distribution, update path, storage backend and capability versioning.
- A check on whether #255 and #284 still count as evidence today.
- A migration path that loses no local data or keys.

title: Agent date refs read chained durations like 66654d0d as today, so a bare hex id fragment can target today's daily note
description:
parseRelativeDate (src/utils/relativeDate.ts) accepts chrono's casual relative-unit chains: '3d' reads as three days ahead, '2d1d' and '1d0d' as a day, and any 'NNNNd0d' string as today. Hex id fragments have that shape: measured on 20,000 random 8-char UUID prefixes, 71 parse whole and about 49 survive the year filter, about 0.25%; '66654d0d', '81092d0d' and '126d3d0d' read as today.

The agent ref resolver (agentViews/resolveRef.ts) tries a bare string as an id, then an alias, then a date. For a write target (append-markdown target, create-block parentId), a non-explicit date may still resolve to an EXISTING daily note (targets.ts, resolveAgentTarget), and today's note almost always exists. So an agent that passes a stale bare 8-char id fragment as a write target can have its content appended under today's note instead of getting 'No block matches'. A ^ or ((…)) prefix forces the id reading and is safe.

Before full-id views (agent views now print whole ids; prefix resolution is removed), a fragment matching a block resolved to that block, and only a fragment matching nothing fell through to the date. Now every fragment falls through. Agents still hold fragments from old transcripts and notes.

Fix direction: make the agent date reading refuse relative-unit chains and bare unit shorthand ('Nd', 'NdMd'), or accept a date only when the input reads as words or an ISO/Roam date. Check the QuickFind and daily-note callers of parseRelativeDate before changing the shared parser. A narrower option is a check in resolveDate alone.

title: Pin the revival rule that treats a created-in-tx row's whole bag as written
description:
`materializeRevivedRow` (src/data/internals/propertyChildrenProcessor.ts) treats the whole bag of a row CREATED in this tx as written by it: `const startBag = baseline === undefined ? row.properties : baseline?.properties ?? {}`. The `null` arm (created in this tx) is what makes such a row's undecodable cell value reject instead of being skipped as untouched legacy data, and what makes its keys reconcile non-additively.

Nothing pins it. The test "treats every key of a revived row CREATED in this tx as written by it" (src/data/propertyChildren.test.ts) writes its junk value with `tx.update(valueRow, {properties: {status: 123}})`, and since eager bag validation landed in `tx.update`, that call throws "Cannot materialize property" itself, before any revival runs. The assertion matches either way.

Reproduction: `pnpm mutate --file src/data/internals/propertyChildrenProcessor.ts --edit "perl -0pi -e 's/const startBag = baseline === undefined \? row\.properties : baseline\?\.properties \?\? \{\}/const startBag = baseline == null ? row.properties : baseline.properties/' \"\$MUTATE_FILE\"" --test src/data/propertyChildren.test.ts` reports UNPINNED.

Fix direction: through the public tx API every unsettled bag write is now validated eagerly, so the junk value can only reach a created-in-tx row through a settled writer. Either pin the rule with a test-only settled same-tx processor that runs before core.materializePropertyChildren and writes the junk bag, or decide the reject arm is defence in depth now, label it at the declaration, and pin the additive-vs-written half (a same-tx child edit under a created-in-tx row that is then subtree-deleted and restored) instead.

title: Annotations: a range anchor can resolve exact on a different repeat of its quote
description:
A range anchor (`src/plugins/annotations/anchor.ts`) stores the quote, the offset it started at, and up to 16 characters of context on each side. It never records which occurrence it means. On text that repeats, an edit can move a quote so that a DIFFERENT occurrence resolves, and sometimes resolves as `exact`, which every write accepts with no confirmation (Accept suggestion included).

Reproduction (measured 2026-11-02, plain edit, no split):

```ts
const R = '0123456789abcdef', T = 'ghijklmnopqrstuv'
const text = (R + 'ship' + T).repeat(3)          // occurrences at 16, 52, 88
const anchor = captureAnchor(text, 52, 56)       // the second one
resolveAnchor('x'.repeat(36) + text, anchor)     // {state: 'exact', from: 52} — the FIRST one; the quoted one is at 88
```

A split does the same in its own way (`splitRetarget.ts`, accepted there with a note): a moved quote's piece can drop the context that picked it, and a repeat wins. Measured: capture the second `ship` in `We can ship Beta tomorrow. We must ship Beta today.`, change `must` to `might` (resolves moved at 36), split right after that `ship`: the piece resolves moved at 7.

How bad it is: `moved` blocks writes until someone confirms, and Confirm position confirms the occurrence that is highlighted, so the user sees the wrong text first. The `exact` case needs a window of quote plus 16 characters each side repeated character for character (templated lines, repeated list items). There, Accept suggestion can change the other copy, which reads the same.

Fix direction (not designed): let a moved anchor survive edits by tracking its offset. Map `quoteStart` through each edit of the target in the same tx (as `followSplitProcessor` does for splits), so `exact` means "the text the user selected" rather than "matching text at the old offset". Size it first: how many live threads resolve moved, and how many quote text that repeats in their target.

title: Decide whether useProperty should read the workspace's resolved property winner
description:
useProperty (src/hooks/block.ts) reads the cell under the schema's own name and decodes with the caller's codec. block.get / peekProperty / tx.getProperty resolve the workspace's winner for the name first (getResolvedProperty in src/data/internals/propertySchemaResolution.ts). The two disagree for a shadowed name (block.get returns the default, the hook decodes the raw cell), for a handle to a renamed user-defined definition (different bag key), and when the winner's codec differs from the caller's.

Routing the hook through the resolver is not a drop-in fix: the resolver fails closed (defaults) for any workspace other than the active or immediately previous one and has a boot-window mode, and useProperty is the hottest render read. Before changing it, size: which useProperty callers pass handles vs plain schemas, whether any rendered block can live in a non-active workspace, and the per-render cost of propertySchemaResolverFor. Also note that the resolver can change without the block changing, so a resolved hook would need to re-read on registry updates.

Done when: either useProperty reads through getResolvedProperty (with those cases tested) or the comment at useProperty records why it stays a raw read.

title: Let block text use full width below attribution badges
description: Contributor attribution, comment indicators, and backlink counts currently use nested flex decorators that reserve width for the full block height. On a multiline block, text below the first line stays unnecessarily narrow. Explore a renderer-owned text-flow seam that lets prose wrap around a compact first-line indicator, while checking headings, other decorators, narrow columns, and edit mode. Keep interactive editors and non-prose renderers coherent; avoid coupling core to specific plugins. Compact contributor labels can ship independently.

title: Comments: retarget threads when a multi-line paste moves a block's suffix
description:
A multi-line paste in the middle of a block moves that block's suffix onto the last pasted block, and a comment thread quoting the suffix goes stale.

Today: pasting several lines mid-text into block B leaves the text before the cursor plus the first pasted line on B. The text after the cursor moves to the end of the last pasted block, which is created in the paste's own transaction ('paste multiline text at editor selection', src/paste/operations.ts around the multiline-paste paths). A thread whose quote was in that suffix still targets B. Its quote is no longer there, so it resolves stale and its highlight disappears.

Splits already handle this. core.split emits core.blockSplit, and the annotations plugin's same-tx processor (src/plugins/annotations/splitRetarget.ts) moves each thread to the block that now holds its text. The paste can't reuse that event as it stands. BlockSplitPiece says each piece is now the WHOLE content of its block, and here the suffix lands at an offset after the pasted text.

Fix direction:
- either give a piece its offset in the destination block (`at`), or emit a separate "text moved" event from the paste;
- have the processor capture the anchor against the destination block's real content at that offset, instead of slicing the event's content;
- text the paste replaced (a non-empty selection) is deleted, not moved, so a thread quoting it goes stale as it does today.

Test: paste two lines mid-text into a block with a thread on its suffix, then assert the thread resolves exact on the last pasted block; undo restores the original target.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #1540); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: Comments: a "what's new" view of unread comments, each with its context
description:
A "what's new" view for comments: the comments a reader hasn't seen yet, each with a little context.

Idea from Max Krieger's "Chatting with Glue" (cited in the design doc's "Nested threads" section): a list of new messages, each shown with just enough context to answer it without opening the whole thread.

Shape to aim for: one entry per unread comment (or per thread with unread comments), showing the target block's text with the quote highlighted, the chain from the thread root down to the new comment with authors (the same root-to-comment chain the agent prompt uses), and a reply box. Opening an entry, or replying, marks it read.

Depends on the read-state decision: "unread" needs per-reader state to exist first. The filtered all-comments view (#1533) is the closest existing piece; this could be one more filter on it ("unread") plus the context rendering.

title: Comments: decide how per-reader read/unread state works
description:
Decide how per-reader read/unread state works for comments (and whether it generalises beyond them).

Context: comments are blocks (`annotation:thread` roots under the `Comments (km)` page, replies nested under the comment they answer). The design doc ("Nested threads") already fixes one rule: per-reader state, meaning unread markers and per-reader collapse, belongs in each user's UI state, never on comment blocks. It also notes that today's collapse is a synced block property, so collapsing a branch collapses it for every reader and device.

Questions to settle:
- Where it lives. A candidate is the user's own `ui-state` block under their user page (`src/data/stateBlocks.ts`), which already holds per-user state and syncs across that user's devices. It must sync per user (one reader on several devices sees one read state), and never land on the shared comment rows.
- Grain. A per-thread "seen up to" timestamp (cheap, one value per thread, compared against `coalesce(user_updated_at, updated_at)` of its comments) versus per-comment read marks (exact, but one record per comment per reader). The timestamp also answers "edited since I read it".
- What marks something read: opening the thread card, scrolling it into view in the margin, or an explicit gesture. And whether a comment you wrote counts as read.
- Agents: whether an agent contributor has read state at all (probably not: the scope recipe already has its own cursor).
- Scope: comments only, or also new backlinks/mentions of a block (the same "what changed since I looked" question).
- Per-reader collapse: whether it moves to the same store.

Done: a short decision recorded in `docs/comments-annotations-design.html` (or a linked doc), with the storage shape and the grain chosen, so the unread markers and the "what's new" view can be built on it.

title: Comments: inline diff for open edit suggestions
description:
Show an open edit suggestion as an inline diff in the target block's text.

Today a suggestion (a thread root with `annotation:replacement`) shows its change as a diff card in the thread/margin, and its span gets the suggestion highlight style. Reading the proposed text in place means opening the card.

Fix direction: a read-mode (and CodeMirror) decoration that renders the quoted span struck through with the replacement beside it, for exact-anchored open suggestions only, with Accept / Reject reachable from it. Display-only: accept and reject keep using the existing transactions.

title: Comments: show a block's mentions in the margin beside its threads
description:
Optionally show a block's plain backlinks as "mentions" in the comments margin, beside its threads.

A note elsewhere that references a block is commentary that happens to live somewhere else. The margin (`src/plugins/annotations/margin.tsx`) shows only `annotation:thread` roots targeting the block today.

Fix direction: a display toggle in the margin that lists the block's backlink sources (the backlinks plugin's sources owner, which already excludes the `annotation:target` edge and thread-root content edges) as mention cards, below or interleaved with its threads. No data-model change; per the design doc ("Comments and references") this sits on top of the thread model, not inside it.
notes: Review-round fixes are ready in https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/1546. Head 4e742699265029f8a5239ebf50816d694e4467a4. Full gate: check: PASS (901 files, 13086 tests). Core dialog isolation, plugin dependencies, panel breadcrumb navigation, query planning and requested cleanups shipped in separate commits. Eleven mutations in this round failed named tests. Screenshots unchanged; PR links pinned to the image commit. No fresh browser QA or live large-graph timings this round. Awaiting merge.

title: Comments: filtered all-comments view (open, by author, by scope)
description:
A filtered view of all comment threads: open only, by author, by scope.

Today the only workspace-wide list is the `Comments (km)` container page, where the thread renderer shows each thread with its target. There is no way to see only open threads, only one contributor's threads, or the threads anchored under one page.

Fix direction: a query view over `annotation:thread` blocks (status from `annotation:status`, author from `attribution:creators[0]` falling back to `created_by`, scope through the same recursive scope read the agent recipe uses in `src/plugins/annotations/scope.ts`), opened from the existing comments action. Filter inside the query, before any limit.

title: Agent mention prompt omits an edit suggestion's replacement
description:
An agent mentioned in a comment thread gets the thread's quote in its prompt but not, for an edit suggestion, the proposed replacement: loadThreadContext (packages/agent-dispatch/src/threadContext.ts) copies thread.quote and thread.anchor from the comments view and drops thread.replacement. So the agent reads 'the thread quotes "X"' with no sign that someone proposed replacing X, and can't discuss or refine the suggestion.

Fix direction: add replacement: string | null to ThreadPromptContext (prompt.ts), copy it from the comments view (already clipped there), and render one line after the quote in renderThreadContext, e.g. It suggests replacing it with: "<replacement>", passed through neutralizeDisplayText like the quote. Test in the dispatch prompt/threadContext tests: a suggestion thread renders the line, a plain thread doesn't.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #1527); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: Read-mode Copy reference on embeds, backlink entries and comment cards
description:
The read-mode selection menu (ReadSelectionMenu in src/plugins/annotations/readSelectionUi.tsx) is mounted inside CommentPill, which applies only to outline blocks (not isNestedSurface). So in an embed, a backlink entry or a comment card there is no right-click menu for selected rendered text. Comment and Highlight refuse off the outline anyway (they open a composer there), but Copy reference runs anywhere: in edit mode it already works on those surfaces.

Fix direction: mount the menu on nested surfaces with only the gestures that run there (a per-gesture flag, e.g. outlineOnly on Comment and Highlight), or a separate nested-surface decorator offering Copy reference. Until then, quoting from those surfaces goes through the editor: click in, select, run Copy reference to selection.
notes: Implemented in https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/1525. The PR remains open for review and merge; leave this issue open until the PR merges. Shared gesture applicability and nested selection-menu regression coverage are included. Real Chrome verification covered the embed menu, outline menu and clipboard write. One adversarial review round found no defects or worthwhile cleanups.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #1524); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: CodeMirror selection and toasts ignore the app's dark theme mode
description:
## Problem

Two UI pieces carry their own light/dark switch and are never told the app's theme mode, so they stay light under every dark theme:

- **CodeMirror editors.** CodeMirror picks its base-theme colours from the `EditorView.darkTheme` facet. Nothing in `src/` sets it, so every editor uses the `&light` base theme. The visible case is the drawn text selection (`.cm-selectionBackground`): no app CSS overrides it, so dark themes would get the light base colour (a pale lavender when focused) behind near-white text. This is reasoned from `@codemirror/view`'s base theme, not measured in the app: check it first by selecting text in a block editor under a dark theme.
- **Toasts.** The sonner `<Toaster>` in `src/extensions/toastAppMount.tsx` has no `theme` prop, so toasts render light under dark themes. They stay readable, just unthemed.

## Fix direction

The active theme's mode is on `<html>` as `data-theme-mode="light|dark"` (set by `src/plugins/theme-toggle/theme.ts` and the `index.html` pre-paint script).

- CodeMirror: either key CSS on it (an editor theme rule like `'[data-theme-mode="dark"] & .cm-selectionBackground'`, since CodeMirror substitutes `&` anywhere in a selector, or token-based colours for the selection), or feed `EditorView.darkTheme` through a compartment that follows the attribute. The CSS route needs no editor reconfiguration on theme change.
- Toaster: pass `theme` from the attribute, or style it with tokens.

Done means: selection and toasts are legible and themed under a dark theme, checked visually in a local dev tab.
notes: Implemented in https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/1518. CSS-driven editor selections and notifications follow the active theme; no subscriptions or editor reconfiguration. Local gate passed, three-theme Chromium visual checks completed, two adversarial reviewers and the quality reviewer found no confirmed issues. Ready for review; leave open until the PR merges.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #1505); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: Wikilinks: entity/escape-decoded alias renders a different target than the indexed edge
description:
A wikilink whose alias contains an HTML entity or a backslash escape is indexed under one name and rendered/resolved under another.

## Reproduction (observed on master, 2026-10-30)

| Source | `parseReferences` alias (the stored edge) | Renderer alias (`remarkWikilinks`, what the link resolves) |
|---|---|---|
| `[[a & b]]` | `a & b` | `a & b` |
| `[[a\*b]]` | `a\*b` | `a*b` |

`parseReferences` scans raw block content. The renderer reads mdast text nodes, which CommonMark has already decoded (entities to characters, `\*` to `*`). So the rendered link resolves a different alias than the reference edge the index stored: it points at a different page or at none, and backlinks disagree with what the link shows.

The single-text-node wikilink pass (the "bare `[[alias]]`" pass in `src/plugins/references/markdown/wikilinks/remark-wikilinks.ts`) has this today. The cross-node pass refuses the case when an inline-HTML node is in the span: it compares against the original VFile source and leaves the span literal, so it at least never resolves the wrong name.

## Fix direction

Derive the alias from the original source slice rather than the decoded text, using node `position` offsets into the VFile, which react-markdown passes. Then index and renderer agree byte-for-byte. Alternatively, decide the decoded form is canonical and decode in `parseReferences` as well. That changes stored edges, so it would need a pass over existing references. The source-slice approach changes no stored data.

Check whether imported content (HTML-escaped titles) actually contains such aliases before prioritising.

title: Multi-select indent/outdent/move bound backlink and embed rows by their page, not their entry
description:
Multi-select indent / outdent / move bound a row selected in Linked References or an embed by the root of its own PAGE. Single-block Tab, Shift+Tab and Alt+Shift+Arrow on the same row bound it by the SURFACE it renders in: a backlink entry's shown block (`BlockEntry.tsx`, `scopeRootId: shownBlock.id`) or the embedded block. So a multi-select step can carry such a row out of its entry while staying in its page, and the row then disappears from the entry.

Reproduce (reasoned from code, 2026-10-30, after #1494): in a backlink entry whose shown block S has children [c1, c2], select c1 and c2 and press Shift+Tab. Both become siblings of S in their page and leave the entry. With one block focused, Shift+Tab on c1 is refused there, because c1's parent is the entry's scope root.

Why it isn't bounded by the entry: the stored selection (`selectionStateProp`, `BlockSelectionState`) holds only block ids, and the multi-select deps carry one `scopeRootId`, the panel's. `applyOutlineGestureToGroupInTx` (`src/data/outlineGroupGestures.ts`) therefore derives a scope root from the tree: the panel root for rows under it, otherwise the row's page root.

Fix direction: record each selected row's surface scope root at selection time and group by it. Every writer knows it except one:
- `toggleBlockInSelection`: the pointer deps' `scopeRootId`;
- vim `v` / Space: NORMAL_MODE deps;
- structural `extendSelection`: its `scopeRootId` parameter.

The exception is spatial navigation's cross-surface ranges (`commitSelectionRange` from `extendSelectionToSpatialTarget`). Their rows come from the DOM with only a render scope id, and deferred slots name no scope at all. They would need the scope root on the row element (DefaultBlockRenderer's shell props), with a fallback for slots. Rows without a recorded scope would keep the page bound.

title: Multi-select move up reorders a selection spanning depths: a block jumps a sibling subtree holding another selected block
description:
Multi-select move up reorders a selection whose blocks sit at different depths: a block jumps a sibling subtree that holds another selected block.

Reproduce (measured 2026-10-29 with the real `multi_select.move_block_up` handler on the test DB, after the group-gesture fix for km-lxf0):

    r1
    r2
      r2a
      r2b   <- selected
    r3      <- selected
    r4

Select r2b and r3 (a visually contiguous range: Shift+Down from r2b), then Move up. Result:

    r1
    r3
    r2
      r2b
      r2a
    r4

r2b swaps above r2a as expected, but r3 swaps above its previous sibling r2, carrying it past r2's whole subtree, so r3 now renders above r2b. The selection is reordered among itself. Move down over the same selection happens to stay in order (r3 goes below r4, then r2b enters r4 as its first child).

This is moveVertical's depth-invariant rule (a block swaps with its whole previous sibling subtree) meeting a group that spans depths; the old per-block fan-out did the same. The group rule in `applyOutlineGestureToGroupInTx` (`src/data/outlineGroupGestures.ts`) keeps runs of selected SIBLINGS whole, and does not cover this.

Needs a decision on what a mixed-depth group move should mean. Options:
- hold a block whose neighbour in the direction of travel CONTAINS a selected block (r3 stays, r2b moves alone: the group stays in order but is split by r2a);
- refuse the whole step when any member would jump another member (all-or-nothing for a mixed-depth group);
- a real group move: move the row above the group's top to below its bottom, which changes the depth of the row that moves.

title: A panel's block selection survives navigating the panel
description:
A panel's block selection survives navigating the panel (zooming into a bullet, following a link), so multi-select mode stays on, acting on ids that may no longer be in the panel's subtree. Example: select [A, B], tap A's bullet. The panel zooms into A, but the selection still holds A (now the view root) and B (not under it). Move down then moves B among siblings the user can't see, and Move to… moves the zoom root itself. Undoable, nothing lost. This predates touch selection (the hazard is noted on `BlocksActionContext` in `src/shortcuts/utils.ts`), but tapping a bullet while selecting on touch makes it easy to reach.

Fix direction: clear the panel's selection when its top-level block changes, in the one place a panel's navigation writes `topLevelBlockIdProp`.

title: one owner for the microtask read batchers
description: src/data/internals/ancestorBatch.ts, src/plugins/backlinks/sourceBatch.ts and src/plugins/annotations/summaryBatch.ts (added for #1469) each hand-roll the same transport: a pending map keyed per request, a flush scheduled with queueMicrotask, the batch taken before the first await so late arrivals open the next one, noteSharedWork when callers share a statement, and a failure that rejects only its own batch. A generic owner (e.g. a createMicrotaskBatcher(key, flush) in src/data/internals) would hold that once; each site keeps only its SQL and grouping. Each batcher's existing tests (sourceBatch.test.ts, ancestorBatch.test.ts, summaryBatch.test.ts) already pin the take-before-await and failure-scoping rules, so they cover the move. Touches core (ancestorBatch.ts), so it is its own PR.
close_reason: Landed in #1493 (src/data/internals/readBatch.ts owns the transport; ancestorBatch, sourceBatch and summaryBatch use it). The PR body did not say Fixes, so the issue stayed open.

title: Live presence: show other members' selections, pointers and carets in a shared workspace
description:
Show, live, where other members of a shared workspace are: the blocks they have selected or are editing, their mouse pointer, and their editor caret. Spike PR #261 (June 2026) built a first version. It was closed unmerged on 2026-10-29 because it had fallen ~4700 commits behind master and still had open review findings. This issue keeps what it learned.

## Design the spike chose (still looks right)

Presence is ephemeral awareness state, not document data. Keep it OFF the persistent path (PowerSync → `blocks` → e2ee → RLS → compaction). A pointer moving 20×/s would become row-write churn, history pollution and lag there.

Use Supabase Realtime, which is already authenticated in the client. It needs no new infra, no table and no migration:
- **Presence** (`track`): identity, selected/focused block ids, editor caret. Low frequency, and it expires on disconnect by itself.
- **Broadcast** (a `cursor` event): the mouse pointer, throttled to ~50 ms.
- One channel per workspace, owned by one module store with **two notification lanes** (presence vs cursor), so the cursor stream never re-runs the selection decorators or the caret recompute.
- Anchor a pointer to a block plus a fractional offset inside it, so it lands on the same logical spot whatever the viewer's scroll or window width.

It used only existing facet seams, with zero core API changes. All of them still exist on master (checked 2026-10-29):

| Seam | Role |
|---|---|
| `appEffectsFacet` | channel lifecycle and the global pointer-move broadcast |
| `panelMountsFacet` | publish the active panel's selection, focus and caret |
| `blockShellDecoratorsFacet` | remote-selection rings around block shells |
| `appMountsFacet` | the pointer overlay |
| `codeMirrorExtensionsFacet` | remote carets (a StateField + ViewPlugin, decoupled from `BlockEditor`) |

## Must-haves the review surfaced before this can ship

- **Private channel (was P1).** The spike joined a public `presence:<workspaceId>` topic. Workspace ids appear in app URLs, so anyone with the public client config could subscribe, read block ids and offsets, or forge presence. Use Realtime Authorization (a private channel, plus an RLS policy on `realtime.messages` that gates joins on `workspace_members`).
- **e2ee workspaces.** Presence sends block ids and caret offsets (metadata, not content) to the Realtime server. Either encrypt the payload with the workspace key, or turn presence off for e2ee workspaces.
- **Treat every remote payload as untrusted.**
  - Drop malformed entries (a missing `userId`, `selectedBlockIds: null`): one bad peer must not break presence for everyone in the channel.
  - Derive a peer's color locally from `userId`. Never interpolate a remote string into `cssText`.
- **One presence key per tab.** The persisted installation `clientId` collapses two tabs of one browser profile into one peer, and makes a client drop its own other tab as "self". Add a per-tab id.
- **Anchor pointers to block shells only.** `[data-block-id]` also marks inline block refs and property rows.
- **Carry the render scope.** The same block can render in split panes, embeds and backlinks:
  - A peer's focus ring should appear only on the copy they are in.
  - A pointer whose scope isn't rendered here should be hidden, not drawn on the first copy.
- **Carets:**
  - Publish `editor: null` when the peer leaves edit mode but keeps focus.
  - Rebuild caret decorations from the latest presence on doc changes. Presence can arrive before the matching content sync, and only mapping an already-clamped DecorationSet loses the offset.
- **Pointer hide:** cancel the trailing throttled move before broadcasting "gone", or a stale pointer reappears up to 50 ms later.

## Open product questions

- Default on or off once hardened?
- Should v1 ship carets, or start with selection rings and pointers only?

## Notes

The spike never ran the gate: its cloud sandbox could not install dependencies. Treat its code as a design reference, not a tested base. It is still readable on the #261 branch.

title: decide one UI deletion rule for kernel container pages
description: Kernel pages that hold records (Properties, Types, Journal, Locations, Assets, Comments (km), plugin roots) have no shared deletion policy. Only the Journal and daily notes (daily-notes deletionGuard.ts) and Comments (km) (annotations container.ts, refuses while it holds threads) refuse a UI delete. Properties, Types, Locations, Assets and SRS Review do not. A delete cascades to the whole subtree, and the next getOrCreateKernelPage restores only the page row, so the records under it stay deleted until an undo or a subtree restore. For Properties and Types that would take user-defined property and type definitions with it. Not verified: whether something else (SeededDefinitionWriteError on seeded definitions) already blocks that delete. Proposal: one rule in core, 'a kernel page that is a container refuses UI deletion while it holds live records', declared once (for example a flag on KernelPageSpec or a container registry) instead of one guard per plugin; the Comments (km) guard would fold into it. First step: measure what deleting the Properties page through the UI does today.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #1471); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: annotations: batch the per-thread summary reads behind the comment pill
description: annotations.threadsForBlock (src/plugins/annotations/summaries.ts) gets thread ids from the batched backlinks statement, but then reads the roots with one statement and each root's visible-child count with one core.childIds statement per thread. Measured on a warm wave of 100 rendered blocks, 30 of them with one thread: 64 statements, 60 of them from the summaries, queued on the 1-2 connection read pool. That is the pattern sourceBatch.ts exists to prevent. Fix direction: answer roots plus visible-child counts for every block in a wave with one batched statement (a sibling of BacklinkSourceBatcher, keyed by workspace and recognition params, with a correlated COUNT using recognizedFieldRowSql), declaring a parent-edge dep per root and row deps through hydrateBlocks. At minimum, one statement per block instead of 1 + threads.
close_reason: Closed on GitHub (issue #1469); reconciled by bd-github-sync.

title: sync: try PowerSync's checkpointMode 'requests' once the service is confirmed to support it
description:
The app syncs with PowerSync's default `checkpointMode: 'legacy'`. After uploads drain, the SDK asks the service to mint a write checkpoint (`/write-checkpoint2.json`). The service bumps one counter per user and returns the number, and the device holds downloads until a checkpoint carries it.

PowerSync JS SDK 2.2+ also offers `checkpointMode: 'requests'`:
- **Allocation:** the device allocates the checkpoint number from its own counter and posts it to `/sync/checkpoint-request`.
- **Reconciliation:** on every connection, the device and the service reconcile by taking the higher counter.
- **Retries:** an unacknowledged request is re-posted every 10 s.
- **`requestCheckpoint()`:** a new call to wait until the server reflects this device's writes.

Why try it:
- After a wipe of the instance's storage, or a move to a new instance, the device re-seeds the service, so checkpoint numbers can't go backwards. That's reasoned from the core's `docs/write-checkpoint-requests.md`, not measured. Under legacy mode a restart lets a stale checkpoint through. PR #1443 closes that with a stopgap trigger (`ps_crud_forget_seen_checkpoint` in `src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts`).
- PowerSync describes the mode as more efficient.

Risk:
- It needs a service that supports checkpoint requests.
- If the reconciliation call fails, the SDK fails the whole download loop (`AbstractStreamingSyncImplementation` in `@powersync/shared-internals`). An unsupported service would break sync, not fall back.

Steps, after #1443 merges:
1. Confirm the PowerSync Cloud instance's service version supports checkpoint requests (PowerSync dashboard or docs).
2. Set `checkpointMode: 'requests'` in the `db.connect(...)` options in `src/data/repoProvider.ts`. Run `writeCheckpointGate.test.ts` in that mode: the test's `takeWriteCheckpoint` helper drives `updateLocalTarget` with a fixed id, so the requests path needs its own probe.
3. On a sandbox account against the real service, check four things:
   - a local write uploads, and its downloads are held until the checkpoint covering it arrives;
   - a second device's write arrives;
   - a reload resumes the stream;
   - nothing breaks when the app is offline at startup.

Done when sync is confirmed working in requests mode against the real service, or the service is found not to support it and that is recorded here.

title: sync: decide per platform between PowerSync's shared sync worker and per-tab sync
description:
The app forces PowerSync's shared sync worker on every platform. `webDatabaseOptions` in `src/data/repoProvider.ts` passes `enableMultiTabs: true` (PR #1443 kept 1.x's behaviour). The 2.x SDK's own default turns it off on Safari, iOS and Android. There it falls back to per-tab sync (`TabLocalStreamingSyncImplementation`): the sync loop runs on the page, and tabs coordinate over broadcast channels. The SDK's comment gives no reason for that default.

The question is whether per-tab sync is the better choice on some platforms, most likely Android and iPhone, where the app runs as a single installed app.
- **iPad:** probably keep the shared worker. It has run there for a long time, and that device class has a history of storage and sync issues that make topology changes hard to attribute.

Investigate per platform (desktop Chromium, macOS Safari, iPhone Safari/PWA, iPad PWA, Android Chrome/PWA):
- **Support:** does `SharedWorker` exist, and does the shared sync worker survive app backgrounding and resume?
- **Main thread:** how much main-thread time does per-tab sync add during an initial sync and during steady editing?
- **Reconnects:** compare reconnect behaviour after the app is suspended. Background: an earlier iPad upload stall was never explained.
- **The suspected hang:** whether a second tab's `connect()` can hang under per-tab sync on Safari. A review raised this; it is unverified.
- **Metrics:** with per-tab sync, the sync engine's DB work shows up in our contention metrics (`src/data/internals/timingMetrics.ts`, `poolInstrumentation.ts`). Check how that changes their meaning.

Done when there is a per-platform recommendation backed by measurements on real devices. If any platform should switch, the change is to stop forcing `enableMultiTabs` there, for example per platform via user agent, and update the pin test `src/data/repoProvider.test.ts` to match.

title: Three component tests copy the same hand-written globalState mock
description:
Three component tests carry a byte-identical 27-line `vi.mock('@/data/globalState.ts', …)`: a hand-copied, peek-based re-implementation of useUIStateBlock / useUIStateProperty / useInFocus / useInEditMode / useIsSelected.

- src/components/references/test/blockReferences.component.test.tsx:50
- src/components/renderer/DefaultBlockRenderer.test.tsx:50
- src/components/renderer/blockContextMenuItemsFacet.test.tsx:38

A copy re-implements the hooks the code under test depends on. It drifts from the real useInEditMode/useInFocus selectors, for example in render-scope matching, and a test can pass against the copy while production differs.

Fix direction: drop the mock and run the real hooks. src/components/test/blockEditorFocusHandoff.test.tsx (PR #1445) does this:
- give each BlockContextProvider a `panelId` whose row is the ui-state block (getUIStateBlock → panelUIStateBlock returns a cached row synchronously);
- render under `<RepoContext value={repo}>`;
- mock only `@/components/Login.tsx` `useUser`.

src/data/test/useUIStateBlock.suspend.test.tsx is earlier precedent. Not yet checked: whether each of the three files' scenarios can switch. If one can't, a single shared helper under src/test/ beats three copies.

title: sync: switch PowerSync transport from the pinned WebSocket to the 2.x default HTTP streaming
description:
PowerSync 2.x changed the default sync transport from WebSocket to HTTP streaming. The 2.x upgrade (#1443) pins `connectionMethod: SyncStreamConnectionMethod.WEB_SOCKET` in the `db.connect(...)` call in `src/data/repoProvider.ts`, so that the upgrade didn't also change transport.

Switching drops that option and puts us on the transport the SDK now tests and documents as its default. 2.x also lazy-loads WebSocket support, so the main bundle may shrink once we stop requesting it.

Why it is separate: a transport change is visible only against the real PowerSync service. Local-only dev tabs never connect, and the test suite drives the core with protocol lines, not a transport.

Done when:
- The pin is removed from `src/data/repoProvider.ts`.
- On a sandbox account against the real service, a local write uploads; a write from a second device or tab downloads; and a reload resumes the sync stream. Check the browser's network panel: no WebSocket, one streaming HTTP request.
- Upload, download and reconnect still work on desktop Chromium and iOS Safari. iOS Safari's streamed-fetch support is the risk to check.

Blocked on #1443 merging.

title: Move the build's React Compiler pass to Babel 8 once babel-plugin-react-compiler supports it
description:
The app build runs the React Compiler through @rolldown/plugin-babel, whose @babel/core peer accepts ^7.29 || ^8. Since the extension compiler moved to @babel/standalone 8 (PR 1439), a root devDependency @babel/core ^7.29.0 keeps that peer on Babel 7: without it pnpm resolves the peer to the @babel/core 8 that @babel/standalone 8 depends on.

Trigger: a babel-plugin-react-compiler release that declares Babel 8 support. 1.0.0 (latest as of 2026-10-24) depends only on @babel/types ^7.26.0. Until then, running it under @babel/core 8 means Babel 7 AST helpers walking Babel 8 ASTs, which changed shape (e.g. ImportExpression, TS nodes).

Fix: drop the root @babel/core pin (or bump it to ^8), rebuild, and diff dist/ against a Babel 7 build. Any difference is React Compiler output for app components and needs review before landing. Babel 7 stays in the tree regardless while eslint-plugin-react-hooks depends on @babel/core ^7.

title: Pull in cooldown-held dependency security fixes after 2026-10-29
description:
The repo resolves dependencies under a 7-day release cooldown (`minimumReleaseAge: 10080` in pnpm-workspace.yaml). Three advisories published 2026-10-23 have fixes that are still too new to resolve.

| package | fixed in | eligible from (UTC) | path | reachable from the shipped app |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fast-uri | 3.1.9 | 2026-10-26 23:05 | @modelcontextprotocol/sdk > ajv | no: local stdio MCP tools |
| happy-dom | 21.0.4 | 2026-10-27 18:05 | devDependency (test env) | no: test-only; also affected on 20.x |
| body-parser | 2.4.0 | 2026-10-29 11:39 | @modelcontextprotocol/sdk > express | no: express never loads (stdio transport only) |

After 2026-10-29 11:39 UTC: run `pnpm up -r`, bump `happy-dom` to ^21.0.4, and confirm `pnpm audit` is clean. Then run `pnpm run check` and commit.

title: Keys typed right after Enter land in the previous block, not the new one
description:
## Observed (2026-10-23)

In a production build (`pnpm build` + `pnpm preview`, local-only login, fresh workspace), editing a block and pressing Enter followed IMMEDIATELY by typed characters puts those characters at the end of the ORIGINAL block. The new block that Enter created stays empty.

- Reproduced on master at 98f97a1e (React 19.2.6) and on the dependency-upgrade branch (React 19.3.1), so it predates that branch.
- Input came from the in-app browser's automation: key events with no delay between the Enter and the first character, on a machine under heavy load (load average ~100 on 12 cores).
- With a ~2 s pause between Enter and typing, the text lands in the new block as expected.

Steps: click into a block's text, End, Enter, type `abc` with no pause, then Escape. The original block now ends in `abc` and the new sibling is empty.

## Not yet known

- How long the window between Enter and the new editor taking focus is at realistic typing speed, and on slower devices (iPhone). Not measured: the repro used 0 ms gaps. Whether a human typing fast hits it is the open question that sets the priority.
- Whether paste or IME composition in that window behaves the same way.

## Fix direction (reasoned, not verified)

The old editor keeps focus until the new block's editor mounts and claims it, and nothing routes input that arrives in between. Two options:
- Stop the old editor accepting input once the split is dispatched (e.g. blur it, or make it read-only, synchronously in the Enter handler) and replay buffered keys into the new editor when it mounts.
- Move focus to a placeholder that belongs to the new block before the async mount.

First measure the window with a timestamped keydown log at the Enter handler and at the new editor's focus.

title: Source provider: let a run read a built-in plugin's authored source at runtime
description:
## Problem

An agent-dispatch run has the km MCP tools and no shell. It can read and write blocks, but it can't read the source of a built-in plugin. A run asked to change something a built-in draws (#1432) has nothing to copy or wrap, unless someone pastes the source into the graph for it.

## Proposal

The source provider from stage 1 of the plugin materialization design (#289, §5.2), landed on its own:

- `src/extensions/pluginSources.ts`: resolve a built-in plugin id (`system:<id>`) to its entry module and submodules and their authored source.
  - In production, fetch the emitted modules' `.js.map` files (stable URLs, since the build uses `preserveModules`) and read `sourcesContent`.
  - In dev, use Vite's `?raw`.
- The relative-to-absolute import rewrite (`./x` to `@/plugins/<id>/x.js`) that a copied entry module needs, since blob modules have no usable base URL.
- A way for a run to reach it: an agent-bridge verb, and a km MCP tool, that return a plugin's sources by id.

## Why

- It's the piece of eject that unblocks graph-only runs today: with it, a run can copy a built-in into an extension and turn the original off (the path #1432 describes).
- It's pure and unit-testable, and eject needs it unchanged later.

## Cost and trigger

Small. Check first that `sourcesContent` survives the current build (react-compiler, the sourcemap settings) before relying on it, since #289 was verified against code on 2026-07-02.

title: Kits: share a page subtree of extensions, types, views and examples as one unit with lineage
description:
## Problem

A useful setup is rarely one extension. A habit tracker is a few extension blocks, a type or two with their properties, a view or saved query, and an example page that shows how to use it. Today there's no way to share that as one thing, and no way for someone who adopted it to receive the author's later fixes.

## Idea, borrowed from Imbue Studio

An Imbue template carries several creations at once: apps, skills, routines and their configuration. Adopting one runs `use-template`, which merges it into a scratch worktree, checks that it boots, and only then fast-forwards the live workspace. Conflicts go to the user. A `template.toml` records `[origin]` and `[[lineage]]`, and `update-self` pulls later changes from the parent template.

Sources: https://github.com/imbue-ai/default-workspace-template (`.agents/skills/use-template/SKILL.md`, `docs/VERSION_HISTORY.md`).

## Sketch

1. A kit is a page subtree: extension blocks, `block-type` and `property-schema` blocks, views or saved queries, and example pages, plus a kit block that names its parts and its version.
2. Publishing exports the subtree. Adopting copies it into the workspace with lineage on the kit block: where it came from, and at which version.
3. Every extension in it arrives disabled and unapproved, like any extension you didn't write. The approval prompt lists the kit's extensions together.
4. Updates reuse upstream tracking per part. An update to the kit is a set of proposals, one per changed block, reviewed together.

## Why

- It's how tools move between people in a malleable medium: whole working setups, not single files.
- It keeps the block grain. A kit is ordinary blocks you can edit, link and undo after adopting it.

## Cost and trigger

Medium to high. It builds on upstream tracking for extensions, which comes first. Once kits pass between people, unreviewed code arrives in bulk, which is the trigger for capability-scoped extensions. Multi-block plugins with imports between their blocks also need stable module URLs for user extensions.

title: Extensions describe themselves: a description on each extension and contribution, listed by describe-runtime
description:
## Problem

An agent that wants to use or change what a workspace can do has to read code to find out. Actions already carry a required description (`Action.description` in `src/shortcuts/types.ts`), and the extension API catalog describes the API surface. Nothing describes what each installed extension contributes: its types, properties, queries, mutators, renderers and actions, or what each one is for.

## Idea, borrowed from Imbue Studio

Each Imbue app publishes what it does: a description in its manifest, and an OpenAPI document generated from its route docstrings. A test fails when a route has no summary, so the description can't go missing. An agent visiting the workspace reads a primer that lists every app and links its API, so it can use an app without reading its code.

Sources: https://github.com/imbue-ai/default-workspace-template (PR 882, an OpenAPI document per app; `visiting-agents.md`).

## Sketch

1. A description on each extension, and on each contribution where the facet allows one: type and property definitions, named queries and mutators, renderers and context-menu items. Keep it short and functional: what it does and when to use it.
2. `kmagent install-extension --verify` warns when an extension or one of its contributions has no description. The same check runs over built-ins in a unit test, the way Imbue's tests refuse a route with no summary.
3. A `describe-runtime` view that lists "what this workspace can do", grouped by extension: built-ins by `system:<id>`, user extensions by block. Each entry shows its description and its contributions.

## Why

- Every later agent run starts better informed: crystallizing a run, fixing an extension, "change this with an agent". Each of them begins by working out what's installed.
- It's cheap, and the required action description shows the rule already works here.

## Cost and trigger

Low. Most of the work is writing descriptions for the built-ins once. Doing it before the agent-facing actions above lets them rely on it.

title: Change this with an agent: a bullet-menu action that briefs a run with what draws the block
description:
## Problem

To change how a block looks or behaves with an agent today, you write a `[[claude]]` mention and explain by hand which block, which types, which plugin draws it, and where that plugin's code lives. The app already knows most of that.

## Idea, borrowed from Imbue Studio

In Imbue Studio you right-click anything and ask the agent to change it. The agent gets the thing you pointed at as its starting context.

Source: https://imbue.com/blog/studio-announce

## Sketch

1. An item on the bullet's right-click menu (the `BlockContextMenuItemsContribution` seam in `src/extensions/blockInteraction.ts`, which "Move to…" already uses): "Change this with an agent".
2. It asks what to change, then starts a run with:
   - the block's id and types,
   - what draws it: the renderer, and the decorators that applied, with each one's contributing plugin (facet contributions carry a `source`),
   - for each of those, whether it's a user extension (an extension block's id) or a built-in (a `system:<id>` toggle).
3. What the run can do depends on what draws the block:
   - **A user extension**: edit that extension's block. The existing drift rule keeps the old source running until you approve the new one.
   - **A built-in**: write an extension that copies the plugin, importing the original's parts through the import map and changing the piece you asked about, then turn the built-in's toggle off. That works today. For todo, other plugins only import its constants, types and action ids, so nothing is left calling the original's code.

## Costs of the "copy and turn off" path today

- **Other devices.** The toggle syncs and the approval doesn't. Until you approve the copy on a device, that device runs neither the built-in nor the copy. No data is touched, and approving the copy there fixes it.
- **Load order.** User extensions load after first paint, so each load briefly shows the block without the copied plugin's parts. The copy's contributions are also appended after the built-ins rather than taking the original's place, which can matter for order-sensitive facets. For example, decorators wrap in contribution order.
- **No record.** Nothing records that the copy replaces the built-in, so nothing tells you when the built-in changes upstream.
- **Source access.** An agent-dispatch run has the km MCP tools and no shell, so it can't read a built-in's source to copy it.

Stage 1 of the plugin materialization design in #289 (an eject action, a `replaces` relation, a source provider) removes all four, so that's the proper version. The source provider alone would unblock runs that can only reach the graph.

## Why

- It turns any block into the place you start changing the software. The context-gathering is exactly what the app knows best and you know least.
- With self-describing extensions, the run can also read what each plugin contributes before it touches anything.

## Cost and trigger

Low for blocks drawn by user extensions. For built-ins it works today with the costs above, and properly once eject exists.

title: Fix with agent: start a repair run from an extension's render or load error
description:
## Problem

When an extension breaks, the app shows it: the render error boundary (`src/extensions/ExtensionRenderBoundary.tsx`) draws an error in place of the block, and a failed load raises a toast (`src/extensions/extensionLoadErrorToast.ts`). Fixing it is then manual. You copy the error, find the extension block, and write a `[[claude]]` mention that explains which extension, what failed and which blocks it was drawing.

## Idea, borrowed from Imbue Studio

Imbue's template has a `heal-creation` skill. When a creation fails, the agent gets the failure and the creation's code and repairs it in the background, the same way it built it.

Sources: https://imbue.com/blog/studio-announce and https://github.com/imbue-ai/default-workspace-template (`docs/system/workspace-internals.md`, creation lifecycle).

## Sketch

1. A "Fix with agent" button on the error boundary's fallback and on the load-error toast.
2. It starts a run with:
   - the error and its stack,
   - the extension block's id and its approved source,
   - for render errors, the id of the block it was rendering and a small sample of the blocks of the same types.
3. The run writes the fix as a new version of the extension's source. It doesn't overwrite the approved pin: the existing drift rule shows `update-available` and the old source keeps running until you approve the change.
