title: strength-tracker: in-progress workout doesn't pick up another device's set edits
description:
Raised by the Codex review on #438 ([thread](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/438#discussion_r3648251326)). Filed rather than fixed there, because the fix is a design change rather than a tweak.

## What happens

`TonightView` reseeds its draft only when the *identity* of the live workout changes — `liveIdentity` is block ids, deliberately. So if the same in-progress session is open on a second device and you tick a set or edit reps there, `liveWorkouts` changes but the identity string doesn't, and the already-open view keeps showing its own values. At Finish it writes its whole draft back, overwriting the other device's edits.

## Why it isn't a one-line fix

Including values in the reseed key would overlay remote values onto whatever you are typing right now — which is exactly what the ids-only key exists to prevent, and the primary use case is one-handed logging at 1am. Doing it properly means per-set dirty tracking: overlay a remote value only for sets this client hasn't touched since its last write, and leave locally-edited rows alone until they're flushed.

## Trigger for building it

Two devices logging the *same* session concurrently. Not observed yet — the realistic pattern is one device per session — so this is deferred rather than scheduled. If it does happen, the symptom is "a set I ticked on my phone came back unticked after finishing on the laptop".

## Sketch

- Track a per-set `dirty` flag set on local edit, cleared once `writeSet` resolves.
- On a live change, overlay values only into non-dirty sets (ids keep working as today).
- At Finish, write only dirty sets rather than the whole draft, so a clean row can't clobber a remote edit.

title: Document export/import round-trip drops all properties (importState replays only content/structure)
description:
### What

The `export_document` / `import_document` global actions (`src/shortcuts/defaultShortcuts.ts`) round-trip a document as JSON, but **properties do not survive the round-trip** — regardless of the properties-as-blocks flip.

`importState` (`src/utils/state.ts`) replays only `id` / `parentId` / `orderKey` / `content`:

```ts
const id = await tx.create({
  id: block.id, workspaceId,
  parentId: block.parentId ?? null,
  orderKey: block.orderKey,
  content: block.content,
})
```

and its input type `ParsedBlock` (`src/utils/markdownParser.ts`) has no `properties` field at all. So `properties` is silently dropped on import even though `export_document` serializes the full block rows.

### Why it's filed now (not fixed in PR #386)

Surfaced while wiring `export_document` to the visible outline in PR #386. It is **pre-existing and orthogonal** to properties-as-blocks — the loss happens under the cell model too. Noting it so it isn't mistaken for a props-as-blocks regression: exporting the visible outline (which #386 does) is correct precisely *because* the machinery representation is per-workspace derived state; the property *values* are lost by `importState` independently.

### Fix direction

Carry `properties` through `ParsedBlock` → `importState`'s `tx.create`. In a flipped workspace, `MATERIALIZE_PROPERTY_CHILDREN_PROCESSOR` would then rebuild the field/value children from the imported bag automatically (it watches `properties`), so no separate child-serialization is needed. Touches the live import path, so it wants an explicit decision before landing.

### Severity

P3: export/import is a manual power-user action, not a sync/backup path, and no data is *destroyed* (the source document is untouched) — the imported copy is just lossy.

title: V8 JSON.parse miscompile trips blockData round-trip fuzz (quarantined from deep tier)
description:
## Summary

`src/data/api/blockData.fuzz.test.ts`'s `blockToRowParams → parseBlockRow round-trips an arbitrary BlockData` property intermittently fails the nightly deep fuzz tier. Root cause is a **V8 `JSON.parse` engine miscompile**, not a product-code defect. Quarantined from the deep tier in PR #390 (pinned to a fixed-seed bounded sample); this issue tracks removing the quarantine once V8 is fixed.

## Why it's an engine bug, not a blockSchema defect

`blockToRowParams`/`parseBlockRow` are a pure `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse` round-trip — correct by construction. The observed failure: a `"` property key decodes to `\` (backslash). Evidence:

- The reported (shrunk) counterexample **passes on replay** — the property is non-deterministic w.r.t. hidden V8 state.
- Regenerating from the seed reproduces at exactly case 20420: `FUZZ_SEED=-915705129 FUZZ_RUNS=25000 yarn vitest run --testTimeout=600000 src/data/api/blockData.fuzz.test.ts -t "round-trips an arbitrary BlockData"`.
- Native, unpatched `JSON.parse` (`=== globalThis.JSON.parse`, `[native code]`). A standalone `node` parses the exact same string **correctly**; a same-shape hand-built string parses fine. Only this one ~486-char input, produced by `JSON.stringify` of a fast-check object, after the deep tier's heavy loop warms the engine, mis-parses.
- Reproduces in vitest and in standalone `node --jitless` (at case 20420); does **not** reproduce in standalone `node` (default JIT) or `--no-opt`.

## Status of upstream filing

No matching V8/Node issue found. Not yet filed upstream: I could not minimize it to a clean fast-check-free repro — hand-built strings with identical content don't trigger it, so it's tied to the specific internal string representation `JSON.stringify` emits plus process/JIT state. A fileable repro would need further reduction (or filed as-is with the fast-check script run under `--jitless`).

## Un-quarantine condition

Restore `fuzzParams(150)` on the property (drop `quarantinedFuzzParams`) once the upstream V8 fix ships in our pinned Node, and confirm the deep tier stays green with the reproducing seed.

See `docs/fuzzing.md` → "When the counterexample passes on replay".

title: Keybinding layers disagree about chord identity: dispatch-dead override spellings still strip live defaults
description:
Found by the PR #384 adversarial review (product-fix correctness lens), deliberately not fixed there (interface-adjacent).

**The gap.** tinykeys dispatch only understands `$mod` and literal `getModifierState` names (`Control`, `Meta`, `Alt`, `Shift`, case-sensitive) — spellings like `ctrl+x`, `cmd+k`, `option+a` never fire. But `canonicalizeChord` folds all of those, and `applyKeybindingOverrides` installs override keys RAW (rule-1 direct override) while using the canonical form for its collision-strip map. So the three layers disagree about what a chord *is*:

- **dispatch** (tinykeys, raw strings): `ctrl+x` is dead
- **strip map** (canonical): `ctrl+x` claims the `Control+x` bucket
- **conflicts UI** (canonical): same bucket

**Concrete failure.** Hand-authored override `ctrl+x` for action B → B's binding is dead at dispatch (pre-existing), but it also strips action A's live default `Control+x` → the chord now does nothing for anyone. Pre-#384 A still fired, so for this input class the (correct) canonical strip made things worse. The settings-UI capture path emits lowercase-but-tinykeys-valid spellings, so this bites hand-authored user prefs / plugin contributions, not captured ones.

**Suggested fix.** Canonicalize override `keys` once at ingestion — the canonical form (`$mod+…`, folded case after PR #384) is tinykeys-valid — so dispatch, strip, and conflict detection agree by construction, and a `ctrl+x` override actually fires. Touches what's stored/round-tripped for overrides, hence a deliberate decision rather than a drive-by: display currently shows the user's spelling.

Related: PR #384's canonicalizeChord case-fold (same review round) closed the `$mod+K`-vs-`$mod+k` slice of this.

title: iPad OPFS SQLite corruption (recurring) — add out-of-band forensic instrumentation
description:
## Summary

The same iPad PWA has now hit **two local OPFS SQLite corruptions within ~24h** (2026-06-30 and 2026-07-01), same 1.4 GB database. Both times **no data was permanently lost** (the server copy + intact local `blocks_synced`/`ps_oplog` had everything; `ps_crud=0`), but the app was left unusable until recovery.

We can diagnose the *end state* well (live remote-inspector forensics), but not the *sequence* that produced it — so we can't yet distinguish the candidate mechanisms. **This issue tracks the incident and adds out-of-band instrumentation so the next occurrence is self-diagnosing.**

Recovery UI for the open-time case shipped in #281 (merged). This is the observability + follow-up tracker.

## Incident #2 forensics (2026-07-01, read-only, on-device)

- Surfaced as a **runtime** error inside the running app: `powersync_control: internal SQLite call returned CORRUPT` (latched in PowerSync `downloadError`; sync-apply crash-loop, `connected:false/connecting:true`). **Not** a DB-open failure — the DB opens fine.
- Full-file OPFS byte scan (347,405 pages × 4096, ~3s) found **exactly ONE fully-zeroed live page** (confirmed not on the freelist), its neighbors pristine. That page begins at byte offset **exactly 1 GiB (2³⁰)**.
- Damaged: the `blocks` table tail (last ~460 of ~341K rows — index-only counts still work, full table scan fails) + FTS5 shadow tables (`blocks_fts_data`/`content`/`rowids`). Everything else intact.
- **Zero data loss:** `ps_oplog` full scan clean (~342K rows, ~211 MB), `blocks_synced` full content scan clean (~342K rows), `ps_crud=0`.
- Ruled out: quota (7% of 41 GB used), a pending hot journal (`-journal`/`-wal` both 0 bytes), random bit-rot (damage is page-aligned + cleanly zeroed at a power-of-two offset), auto_vacuum (off).
- Consequence metrics: the crash-loop saturates the single wa-sqlite thread → app queries run 9–23s.

## Root cause — hypotheses only (not settled)

The mechanism is **not proven**. Candidates:
1. Non-durable OPFS `flush()` on iOS process suspend/kill.
2. A **WebKit-OPFS write/durability bug at the file-size/extent boundary** (the exact-1 GiB alignment leans here — a random killed-mid-write would lose an arbitrary in-flight page, not specifically the 2³⁰ one; a lone zeroed page at exactly 2³⁰ is a 1-in-347K coincidence otherwise).
3. A wa-sqlite `OPFSCoopSyncVFS` coop-lock / handle-close-on-background issue.
4. Coincidence.

The end-state alone can't discriminate these — hence instrumentation.

### External corroboration (known class)
- PowerSync reports ~40 corruption reports / ~40K users ("database disk image is malformed", OPFS VFS, disproportionately Safari/iOS).
- PowerSync documents that `OPFSCoopSyncVFS` access handles get closed when the app is backgrounded.
- A ~400 MB FTS5 WASM DB was corrupted "semi-reliably" by killing the process mid-write (SQLite forum).
- `PRAGMA fullfsync=ON` helped **native** iOS SQLite (survived 10 hard-reset loops) but is a **no-op for wa-sqlite/OPFS** (JS VFS over `SyncAccessHandle.flush()` — durability is whatever WebKit does, un-tunable via PRAGMA).

## Proposed instrumentation (this issue)

All forensic state lives **outside** the OPFS SQLite file (IndexedDB, via the existing `IdbKeyedStore`), stays small (ring-buffered), and is sampled — because the thing we're debugging is the SQLite file being corrupt.

1. **Auto forensic snapshot on `SQLITE_CORRUPT` detection** (open *or* runtime): before any recovery, capture the bundle we gather by hand — OPFS zero-page scan + offsets, which tables fail, `ps_buckets`/`downloadError`, OPFS inventory + sizes, quota, freelist, DB size — and persist it (+ offer download). Turns every future incident into a rich report with no live-inspector session.
2. **Unclean-shutdown flag + lifecycle log:** set `cleanShutdown=false` at startup, `true` on `pagehide`; a still-`false` value on next boot ⇒ the process was killed. Log `visibilitychange`/`freeze`/`resume` timestamps. This is what **discriminates the process-kill hypothesis** (correlate unclean shutdown ↔ later corruption).
3. **Periodic cheap zero-page scan + DB-size log** (startup/idle; ~3s over 1.4 GB, not full `integrity_check`): catches corruption *near when it happens* and records **DB size at corruption** across incidents to directly test the 1 GiB-boundary hypothesis.

Follow-up (not in the first cut): a write-transaction breadcrumb ring buffer (last N tx boundaries: kind, op count, DB size at commit, checkpoint opid).

## Related / out of scope

- **#281 detection gap (separate follow-up):** recovery detection is DB-*open*-scoped only (`toLocalDbOpenError` at `ensurePowerSyncReady`) and `CORRUPTION_SUBSTRINGS` omits `"internal SQLite call returned CORRUPT"` — so this runtime class opens fine and the recovery UI never fires. Widen detection to runtime sync errors + add the phrasing.
- **Bigger durability levers (need a spike, not a blind swap):** `AccessHandlePoolVFS` + WAL (more torn-write-resilient, single-tab) or `IDBBatchAtomicVFS` (atomic commits, but degrades >100 MB / Safari call-stack errors — not viable at 1.4 GB); shrinking the DB (history/tombstone pruning, VACUUM) buys maybe ~30%.
- Consider filing an upstream PowerSync/WebKit report — the "single zeroed page at exactly 1 GiB" fingerprint is more specific than the public reports.

title: Direct writes to `blocks` table don't trigger handle invalidation (stale in-memory cache)
description:
## Summary

Direct writes to the local `blocks` table (outside `repo.tx` and outside the sync ingress) do **not** trigger query-handle invalidation. Nothing watches `blocks`. The in-memory loader-handle cache (and any UI subscribed to it) goes stale until an unrelated overlapping invalidation fires or the client reloads.

## How invalidation actually works today

There are exactly two paths that produce a `ChangeNotification` → `handleStore.invalidate(...)`:

1. **Local writes** — synchronous, no observation involved. `repo.tx` records a per-id snapshots map during its primitives and, post-commit, calls `handleStore.invalidate(snapshotsToChangeNotification(snapshots, rules))` directly (`src/data/repo.ts:1164`).
2. **Sync writes** — PowerSync lands rows in `blocks_synced`; `AFTER INSERT/DELETE` triggers enqueue `(seq, id, op)` into `blocks_synced_changes`; the sync observer subscribes via `db.onChange({ tables: ['blocks_synced_changes'] })` (`src/data/internals/syncObserver/observer.ts:270`), drains the queue, materializes into `blocks`, and calls the **same** `snapshotsToChangeNotification` + `handleStore.invalidate(...)` (`src/data/internals/syncObserver/invalidate.ts:59`).

The only `onChange` subscription in the data layer is on `blocks_synced_changes`. There is **no** watcher, queue, or invalidation trigger on `blocks` itself.

This is deliberate — `src/data/internals/handleStore.ts:1026`:

> Note: `tables` is intentionally NOT auto-emitted. The `kind:'table'` dep mechanism is still wired through `handleStore.invalidate(...)`, but no production query depends on it — auto-emitting `['blocks']` on every commit walked the channel for nothing.

So the effective invalidation contract is: **a write is observed iff it goes through `repo.tx` or arrives via the `blocks_synced` sync ingress.** A raw `UPDATE blocks …` outside those paths fires no handle invalidation.

## Scope / nuance

- **SQL-side derived state stays consistent.** There *are* `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` triggers on `blocks`, but they maintain derived tables (`row_events`, `block_aliases`, `block_types`, `blocks_fts`, `uploads`) — not handle invalidation (`src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts:419`–`925`). So a direct write keeps aliases / type index / FTS correct; only the **in-memory handle cache** goes stale. This is a stale-view bug, not data corruption.
- **Likely a regression introduced by e2ee Layout B (needs confirmation).** In a vanilla PowerSync setup the app reads from the PowerSync-managed table and `onChange`/`watch` (SQLite update-hook backed) fires for *any* write to it, including out-of-band SQL. Layout B split the read table (`blocks`, plaintext) from the sync table (`blocks_synced`, ciphertext), moving the watch to the sync ingress and re-plumbing local-write invalidation onto the explicit `repo.tx` call. The property "any write to the read table is observed" was dropped as a side effect. (The current gap is code-verified; the "this worked pre-Layout-B" comparison is inferred from PowerSync's default reactive model, not from reading the Layout-A code — should be confirmed.)

## Blast radius

Small in normal operation: all app code writes via `repo.tx`, and remote changes flow through `blocks_synced`. The only writers that hit the gap are **out-of-band raw SQL**: the agent bridge `sql execute`, `__omniliner.repo.db.execute`, manual debugging. Those can self-recover today by calling `handleStore.invalidate({ tables: ['blocks'] })` or reloading (the bridge has a `reload` verb).

## Options to consider

- **Do nothing / document the contract** — codify "writes must go through `repo.tx` or the sync ingress" as the invalidation contract; treat raw `blocks` writes as unsupported.
- **Symmetric trigger+queue on `blocks`** — add a `blocks_changes` trigger + a second `onChange` so local writes flow through the same queue as sync writes. Downsides: loses the synchronous, before+after-snapshot precision of the current `repo.tx` fast path (queue carries only id+op, throttled), so it would be a *fallback* for out-of-band writes rather than the primary path.
- **Make the agent bridge's mutating verbs self-invalidate** — have `sql execute` / `eval` emit a coarse `handleStore.invalidate({ tables: ['blocks'] })` (or reload) after a raw write, closing the most realistic real-world gap without touching the hot path.

## TODO

- [ ] Confirm whether pre-Layout-B (Layout A) actually observed direct `blocks` writes (verify the regression claim against the old code).
- [ ] Decide between documenting the contract vs. closing the gap (and at which layer).

title: Empty-plaintext envelope boundary (blank block content) is untested
description:
**Severity:** Low · **Area:** sync/crypto (envelope) · **Status:** confirmed (missing test) · **Audit:** `docs/correctness-audit-2026-06-18.md` (B5)

## Summary
The empty-plaintext envelope boundary (a blank block's `content`) seals to exactly the 28-byte floor (`NONCE_BYTES + GCM_TAG_BYTES`). The decode floor is `< 28` so it passes today, but nothing tests it — a future off-by-one (`<= 28`) would quarantine every empty block on download.

## Where
- `src/sync/crypto/envelope.ts` (`decodeEnvelope` length floor)
- `src/sync/crypto/aead.test.ts`, `envelope.test.ts` (never seal `''`)

## Proposed fix
Add a `seal('') → open === ''` round-trip test and a `decodeEnvelope` truncation test over `[0..28)` bytes to pin the floor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Test: empty-string content column round-trips (`open(seal('')) === ''`).
- [ ] Test: truncated envelopes below the floor are rejected.
- [ ] `yarn run check` green.

title: Workspace-key paste with internal whitespace/newline throws instead of being cleaned
description:
**Severity:** Low · **Area:** sync/crypto (workspace-key paste UX) · **Status:** confirmed · **Audit:** `docs/correctness-audit-2026-06-18.md` (B4)

## Summary
A workspace-key paste containing internal whitespace/newline (line-wrapped paste, printed-on-paper backup) throws `base32: invalid input` — only the outer string is trimmed. A valid backup looks corrupt. No data loss, but a recovery-UX failure for the exact "legible on paper / retyped" case the format is meant to support.

## Where
- `src/sync/crypto/base32.ts:17-23`
- `src/sync/keys/workspaceKey.ts:35` (only outer `trim()`)

## Proposed fix
Strip all internal whitespace from the WK string before base32-decode (in `parseWorkspaceKey`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Test: a WK with internal spaces/newlines parses to the same key as the unwrapped form.
- [ ] `yarn run check` green.

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): low-priority perf misc (logging, copy N+1, bootstrap writes)
description:
Lowest-priority unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit.

1. **`serializeSelectedBlocks` issues one subtree SQL query per selected block (N+1) and can duplicate overlapping subtrees** — `src/utils/copy.ts:63` — multi-block Cmd+C runs N independent `subtree().load()` calls and emits overlapping descendant rows twice. Dedup by hierarchy (`validateSelectionHierarchy`) then fetch in one query.
2. **Independent get-or-create bootstrap page writes run strictly sequentially** — `src/bootstrap/workspaceBootstrap.ts:154-167` — Properties/Types/Recents pages have no mutual dependency yet are awaited serially on the TTI path; `Promise.all` them. Caveat: `repo.tx` serializes on the single wa-sqlite write lock, so the clear win is the warm path (overlapping 3 read round-trips) + collapsing stacked await latency. (Companion to the cold-start DDL round-trip issue.)
3. **`console.debug` string-building in the per-chunk upload path** — `src/services/powersync.ts:347` (also `:313`, `:326`) — argument expressions evaluated regardless of whether debug logging is surfaced; per-chunk (not per-row) so bounded. Gate behind a dev flag. Lowest priority.

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, misc group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): bundle/build payload - minify, lazy-load tutorial extensions
description:
Unverified build/bundle candidates from the 2026-06 audit. (The two biggest individually-tracked bundle wins — `@babel/standalone` and the `lodash` barrel — have their own issues.)

1. **Unbundled, unminified build ships ~11.7 MB raw JS across 1,152 preloaded files with a 117 KB index.html** — `vite.config.ts:148` — `preserveModules:true` (load-bearing for extension `@/` imports) + `minify:false` (an independent choice) + `sourcemap:true`; the 117 KB HTML parses before boot and unminified JS is several-fold larger to transfer/parse. **Highest-leverage item in this group:** flipping `minify:false` (terser preserves export names, so module URLs/named exports are unaffected) is the cheap safe win; optionally bundle+minify the vendor subtree extensions never import by path. Confidence medium on the vendor-bundling half.
2. **Tutorial-only example-extension source strings (~15.5 KB) eagerly bundled into the startup chunk** — `src/extensions/exampleExtensions.ts:1` — pulled in via a static import in `defaultShortcuts.ts:35` (core startup) + `tutorial/outline.ts:19`; used only by the tutorial / a rarely-invoked action. Lazy-load with `await import('@/extensions/exampleExtensions.js')` inside the handler.

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, bundle group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): bulk sync/reprojection - window large passes & id loads
description:
Unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit — two bulk passes hold large in-memory sets / unbounded txs instead of windowing like the download observer (`DEFAULT_DRAIN_CHUNK=1000`).

1. **`materializeWorkspace` loads every workspace id into one array before windowing** — `src/data/internals/syncObserver/observer.ts:227` — `SELECT id FROM blocks_synced WHERE workspace_id=?` with no LIMIT, held as one array (320k strings for a large workspace) for the whole windowed drain, partially defeating the "keep memory flat" intent. Page with a keyset cursor. Runs only on unlock/reconcile/recovery — rare.
2. **Whole-workspace ref reprojection runs in one unbounded `repo.tx`** — `src/data/repo.ts:1488` — `reprojectRefTypedProperties` funnels all matched rows through a single tx (builds the entire snapshots map in memory, holds the writer for the whole pass, emits one giant ps_crud tx), unlike the download observer which windows at 1000. Marker-gated/idle-deferred/add-only, so only bites the first cold start after a new ref-typed schema over a large graph. Window into chunks.

## Related
#91 (parallel reads for cold-start contention).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, bulk-ops group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): references/backlinks post-commit processing - batch lookups, avoid redundant second writes
description:
Unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit in the references/backlinks post-commit processors.

1. **`parseReferences` resolves alias targets one-at-a-time with serial awaited DB lookups per content edit** — `src/plugins/references/referencesProcessor.ts:139` — N distinct wikilinks → N sequential awaited `aliasLookup` round-trips (plus a seat-probe on miss, `:152`) post-commit. Off the typing path and handle-cached, so bulk-paste of many distinct new wikilinks is the trigger. Batch with `WHERE alias IN (...)` or `Promise.all`.
2. **`normalizeReferences` same-tx processor issues a second full-row UPDATE (and second row_events row) when references are not canonical** — `src/data/internals/normalizeReferencesProcessor.ts:48` — short-circuited by `referencesEqual` when already canonical; compounds with the `tx.update` wide-SET issue and `row_events` (#132). Fix the wide-SET issue first (narrow SET) so this second write only touches `references_json`.
3. **Reference-changing edits trigger a second full commit-pipeline pass** — `src/plugins/references/referencesProcessor.ts:266` — a ref-set-changing edit opens its own `repo.tx` writing `{references}`, re-running the whole pipeline (a second `handleStore.invalidate` walk, a second `command_events` row, an extra ps_crud entry). Largely inherent to the deliberate post-commit-separate-tx design; the realistic mitigation is the inverted index (#80) + alias-batching, not removing the second tx. Recorded as structural cost, not a bug.

## Related
- The `tx.update` wide-SET issue (item 2 compounds with it).
- #80 (HandleStore inverted index — reduces item 3's cost).
- #132 (row_events write size).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, references group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): getEffectiveActions recomputed in hot dispatch/render paths
description:
Unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit — the effective-action list (a nested action×transform loop + a fresh ~100-element array) is rebuilt in several hot paths instead of being read from a memoized source.

1. **Pointer/imperative dispatch re-runs the full transform+override pipeline (and re-allocates the list) on every click** — `src/shortcuts/HotkeyReconciler.tsx:242` — `dispatchPointerAction` / gesture dispatchers / `runActionById` (`runAction.ts:46`) each call `getEffectiveActions(runtime)` fresh, though `HotkeyReconciler` already holds the identical list memoized (`:158`). Read a memoized list via a ref, or memoize `getEffectiveActions` at module level keyed on facet identities.
2. **`MobileBottomNav` rebuilds the effective-action list + a Map on every render, and re-renders on every block focus change** — `src/plugins/mobile-bottom-nav/MobileBottomNav.tsx:50` — `getEffectiveActions` + `new Map(...)` in the render body; subscribes to `useActiveContextsState()` which changes on every focus/edit transition. `useMemo` keyed on `[runtime]`.
3. **`useRegisteredAction` runs the full effective-action pipeline in render with no memoization** — `src/plugins/left-sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:57` — `getEffectiveActions(runtime).find(...)` in render per `SidebarAction`; the sidebar renders only a handful and is a toggle surface, so impact is small. `useMemo` on `[runtime, actionId]` or rely on a module-level cache.

The clean fix for all three is one shared memoized `getEffectiveActions` keyed on facet identities (the reconciler already proves the memo key works).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, action-pipeline group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): React render-path memoization & viewport-mount cleanups
description:
Lower-ranked render-path candidates from the 2026-06 audit, **not individually adversarially verified**. Grouped; each is independently actionable.

1. **No `React.memo` anywhere on the block render path** — `src/components/BlockComponent.tsx:16` — a structural edit invalidates the parent's `childIds` handle → `BlockChildren` re-renders → recreates every `<LazyBlockComponent>` → every mounted sibling re-renders down to a full markdown reparse. Confidence medium on the exact re-render trigger set; `React.memo(BlockComponent)` is safe and strictly beneficial. (This is the page-wide fan-out the markdown-reparse issue's medium-downgrade is conditional on.)
2. **Markdown render config reallocated with fresh identities every render** — `src/components/renderer/MarkdownContentRenderer.tsx:35` — fresh `remarkPlugins[]`/`components{}` + an O(references) wikilink Map rebuild per render; the structural blocker that keeps the markdown-reparse memo from being effective. `useMemo` keyed on `[resolveMarkdownConfig, block, blockContext, references]`. (Prerequisite for the markdown-reparse issue.)
3. **Wikilink display decorator runs unmemoized for every wikilink every render** — `src/plugins/references/markdown/wikilinks/Wikilink.tsx:28` — `resolveWikilinkDisplay` loops all decorators per wikilink per render; the daily-date decorator calls `parseLiteralDailyPageTitle` + `pickBlockDateAdapter` (each `canHandle` reads `block.peek()`). Memoize per `(alias, blockId)`.
4. **`useRenderer` runs an unmemoized registry filter+sort (incl. ReactPlayer URL regex) per block per content edit** — `src/hooks/useRendererRegistry.tsx:14-42` — explicit `'use no memo'`; `Object.values(registry).filter(canRender).sort(priority)` per render. Bounded by registry size (~13), constant-factor. Cache the choice keyed by `(rendererKey, types, context flags)`.
5. **`LazyViewportMount` keeps a live `ResizeObserver` per mounted block for its whole lifetime** — `src/components/util/LazyViewportMount.tsx:60-71` — a mounted block never reverts to a placeholder, so continuous observation (a forced `offsetHeight` read on every reflow) is wasted after the first measurement. Measure once or `disconnect()` after first non-zero measurement.
6. **`LazyViewportMount` module-level caches grow unbounded and force eager remount** — `src/components/util/LazyViewportMount.tsx:7-8,38,43` — `mountedCacheKeys`/`measuredHeights` are never pruned (leak) and always-eager-on-revisit (`:38`) re-incurs the O(N) initial-mount cost the lazy wrapper exists to avoid. Bound the caches; still gate mount on the IntersectionObserver.
7. **Per-block window resize/orientationchange listener even when no gesture recognizer applies** — `src/extensions/continuousGestures.ts:680` — `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeViewport, ...)` adds 2 window listeners per mounted block even when `recognizers.length===0` (desktop default), unlike the shared-listener pattern in `keyboardViewport.ts`. Gate on `recognizers.length>0` with a stable module-level no-op subscribe.

## Related
- The markdown-reparse issue (items 1–2 are its prerequisites).
- #74 (per-block flicker on lazy hierarchical loads — useTransition).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, render-path group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06: BlockCache snapshots - unbounded growth + redundant per-write JSON.stringify fingerprinting
description:
Two related issues in `src/data/blockCache.ts`.

## 1. Unbounded snapshot map (verified, low)
`src/data/blockCache.ts:95` — the per-id `snapshots` Map only removes entries on hard-delete (`deleteSnapshot`, `:186`) or `markMissing` (`:240`); every block loaded via query hydrate or `repo.load` stays as a deep-frozen full `BlockData` forever. Hydration paths (`repo.ts:440-453, 519, 888, 896`) add on every paged document, so a long-lived session accumulates without bound. `docs/perf-baseline.md:390-395` estimates ~3 KB/block (~150 MB at 50k blocks), **but** the memory bench came back GC-noisy and the doc flags it needs a steadier harness — magnitude unverified, and 50k distinct blocks in one uninterrupted session is the upper tail.

**Fix:** bounded LRU keyed on entries with no active `BlockCache.subscribe` listeners (`trackedIds()` at `:211` already exposes the seam, zero current callers). Eviction is lossless — the snapshot is written **after** the SQLite commit (`commitPipeline.ts` STEP 6), so the next read re-hydrates the identical value via `applyIfNewer`.

**One edge:** synchronous `block.data`/`peek()` readers (`hooks/block.ts:83-99`) holding a `Block` without subscribing would throw `BlockNotLoadedError` if their snapshot is evicted mid-use — "evict unsubscribed only" mitigates but doesn't fully eliminate this. Effort: medium.

## 2. Double full JSON.stringify per write (unverified candidate, low)
`src/data/blockCache.ts:14-15,128-143` (also `:132`) — `setSnapshot` does two full `JSON.stringify` of the whole block per cache write for dedup, including re-fingerprinting the *existing* snapshot though it can't have changed. `applyIfNewer` already gates on `updatedAt <=` before delegating, so only the local commit path genuinely needs the dedup.

**Fix:** store the fingerprint alongside the snapshot; skip it where the snapshots map already proves the row changed.

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (BlockCache eviction, verified; + fingerprint candidate, unverified)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06: block markdown re-parsed per render - confirm React Compiler doesn't already memoize before fixing
description:
## Location
`src/components/renderer/MarkdownContentRenderer.tsx:35` / `:39`

## ⚠️ Verify-first (cross-area disagreement)
The `react-rendering` audit area **retracted** this finding after running `babel-plugin-react-compiler` (enabled at `vite.config.ts:45`) on the compiled output and concluding the compiler auto-memoizes the `<Markdown>` element and `markdownConfig`. Two other areas verified the mechanism at source level but did **not** reconcile against the compiled artifact. **Before any manual fix, confirm against compiled output whether the React Compiler already memoizes this.** If it does, this is a no-op. If it doesn't (e.g. because the freshly-allocated config identity defeats the compiler's dependency tracking), the fix below applies.

## Problem
`MarkdownContentRenderer` calls `runtime.read(markdownExtensionsFacet)` then `resolveMarkdownConfig({block, blockContext})` on every render with no memoization (`:35-36`), then passes the result into react-markdown's synchronous `<Markdown>`. `resolveMarkdownRenderConfig` (`src/markdown/extensions.ts:29-53`) allocates a fresh `remarkPlugins` array + `components` object and invokes every extension factory each call (wikilink rebuilds a fresh `refMap` per call, `wikilinks/index.tsx:29`). react-markdown's `Markdown` export rebuilds the unified pipeline, re-lexes/parses, runs all remark transformers, and rebuilds the React tree on every call with zero cross-render memoization.

## Why it matters
Runs for any visible block whose parent panel/shell re-renders for an unrelated reason; amplified by breadcrumb/backlink panels that render a full `BlockComponent` per segment (`BreadcrumbList.tsx:86`). There is no `React.memo` in the `BlockComponent → DefaultBlockRenderer → ContentSlot → MarkdownContentRenderer` chain.

Severity: verified at source level, adjusted high → **medium**. The "full re-parse per keystroke" claim is **wrong** — the editing dispatcher (`plain-outliner/interactions.tsx:26-29`) swaps to the CodeMirror renderer while `inEditMode`, so `MarkdownContentRenderer` is not mounted for the block being actively edited; the re-parse happens once on edit-mode exit/commit, not per character. The remaining real cost is per-block re-parse on **parent-triggered** re-renders.

## Fix (if not compiler-handled; medium)
`useMemo` the `markdownConfig` keyed on the resolver identity (the facet `read` is cached per facet id, `facet.ts:188-189`) plus the reactive fields the extensions read — **content + references + workspaceId** (wikilink reads `data.workspaceId`; the original `[content, references, markdownConfig]` key is incomplete). Then wrap the `<Markdown>` subtree in a memo. The config-identity stabilization (tracked in the React render-path grab-bag) is a hard prerequisite — a memo keyed on the freshly-allocated `remarkPlugins`/`components` would never hit.

## Effort
Medium (gated on the verify-first step).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (finding 8, verified at source level; see the cross-area note)._

title: Audit A1 (rescoped): row_events is deliberate history — optimize storage / retention without losing reconstructability
description:
## Status (rescoped 2026-06-12)

Owner correction to the original audit finding: `row_events` is the **deliberate client-side history** — it stays, for all workspaces. The audit facts stand (zero runtime readers since `rowEventsTail.ts` was deleted in 588937cd; full before+after row JSON per write; the measured 262 MB / 304k-row growth case), but the conclusion changes: this is a storage-optimization-and-retention issue, not a remove-dead-machinery issue. Eventual work, not urgent.

## Optimization candidates — all must preserve full reconstructability

1. **Stop storing `before_json` where it's derivable.** The triggers see every write, so an event's `before_json` equals the previous event's `after_json` for the same row. Storing only `after_json` roughly halves the table while losing zero history. Caveats: each chain needs a base (rows whose first event predates trigger installation keep `before_json` on that first event, or get a one-time snapshot event), and any retention trim must keep a base snapshot per surviving chain.
2. **Stop re-embedding unchanged large columns** — `properties_json`/`references_json` are copied in full into both sides even when the write touched neither.
3. **Retention/compaction** — tracked in #75; high-watermark startup-DELETE sketch in `docs/row-events-retention.md`. Compact, never silently drop — history preservation is paramount.

## Trigger

Pick up when DB-size alerts from the health monitoring fire, or before targeting storage-constrained devices. The 262 MB case is the existing evidence of the growth rate.

Related: #75 (retention), #76 (local-only ps_crud).

---
*Source: audit finding A1 (`docs/architecture-audit-2026-06.md`), rescoped per owner correction 2026-06-12.*

title: Test-suite quality: remove source-literal tautologies & brittle over-mocking (audit follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to the test-suite audit. #107 already deleted many pure contribution-list / shortcut-string-restatement tests. The items below are the **tautologies and brittle mocks that survived** that pass — tests that restate a source literal (so they can never catch a real regression) or couple to an implementation detail (so they fail for the wrong reason).

> Per AGENTS.md: "don't add tests that just re-state the code." This is the inverse-direction cleanup.

### Source-literal restatements
- [ ] **`src/data/api/changeScope.test.ts:13`** — `Object.keys(CHANGE_SCOPE_POLICIES)).toEqual(Object.values(ChangeScope))`; the `satisfies Record<ChangeScope, …>` annotation already enforces this at compile time.
- [ ] **`src/data/blockSchema.test.ts:43`** — exact column-name-list `toEqual`. Keep only the `not.toContain` migration guards (~L58–60).
- [ ] **`src/data/internals/clientSchema.test.ts:~216`** — trigger-*name* inventory restatement. (#107 added trigger-*behavior* tests to this file but left the name list.)
- [ ] **`src/extensions/test/config.test.ts`**, **`src/plugins/geo/blockTypes.test.ts`**, **agent-cli `packageManifest.test.ts`**, and the **srs-rescheduling SM-2.5 parameter-list** assertion — same restate-the-constant pattern.

### Over-mocking / brittle coupling
- [ ] **`src/data/internals/kernelMutators.test.ts:296`** — `vi.spyOn(TxImpl.prototype, 'childrenOf')` then asserts not-called; passes silently if the method is renamed or inlined.
- [ ] **`src/extensions/test/discoverToggleTree.test.ts:125`** — `toEqual(['system:dup', 'system:dup'])` *codifies* accidental non-dedup; a future real dedup fix would fail this for the wrong reason.
- [ ] **`src/components/BlockProperties.component.test.tsx`** — asserts a raw `'fixed'` CSS class string (couples the test to styling).

🤖 Tracked from the test-suite audit · https://claude.ai/code/session_01Qb9hPUtry6z6YrC4hf9EyB

title: Consider DB/query revisioning if dirty-load handle semantics become hard to reason about
description:
## Problem

`LoaderHandle` treats in-flight loads that observe a matching invalidation as **dirty** for subscriber publication: the dirty result may still satisfy the original `load()` promise and update the internal cache, but subscribers rebuild only from the clean follow-up reload. This is intentionally conservative and cheap.

## Current state (verified)

The dirty-load model is in place and unchanged in `src/data/internals/handleStore.ts` (mid-load invalidations set `pendingReinvalidate` and schedule a post-settle reload). There is **no** monotonic DB/query revision/version counter.

## Longer-term shape (only if this area keeps producing edge cases)

Add a monotonic DB/query revision model. Every local commit and row-events-tail apply advances a revision; query loads carry the revision they read; handles publish only results whose read revision is at least the latest matching invalidation revision. That makes freshness explicit and could avoid redundant dirty reloads when a load is provably already fresh.

Costs: thread revision accounting through repo txs, sync-applied invalidations, query loaders, and tests; dynamic deps still need the existing "changes during load" queue unless queries can declare every relevant dep before SQL.

**Trigger:** do this only if the dirty-load generation model becomes ambiguous in practice.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until trigger)._

title: Investigate referencesProcessor.test.ts schema-swap flake
description:
## Problem

`src/plugins/references/test/referencesProcessor.test.ts > parseReferences — schema-swap reprojection > removes stale field refs when a property stops being ref-typed` fails intermittently in the full suite but passes in isolation (`yarn test --run src/plugins/references/test/referencesProcessor.test.ts` is green). Observed once during the navigation refactor on master @ `cf397f0`. The failing assertion checks `references_json` for a stale `target-a` ref that should have been removed when the `reviewer` property was retyped away from `block-ref`.

## Current state (verified)

The test still exists (no `.skip` / `.only`), asserting via the existing `vi.waitFor(...)` quiescence pattern on `references_json`. No new retry / timeout / quiescence logic has been added — the flake is not yet patched.

## Direction

The shape suggests an ordering race: alongside the rest of the suite, the property-type cleanup fires before/after the assertion's `vi.waitFor` window in a way the in-isolation run doesn't trigger. Likely candidates: a shared trigger-flush queue across tests in the same vitest worker, or a `repo.tx` racing the schema-swap delete.

Worth instrumenting next time it fails: dump `references_json` history for `src` plus the `row_events` trail across the swap window. If the pattern matches `cycle-detection-test-flake.md`, the fix may be the same shape (await processor quiescence before asserting).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3)._

title: Block-id keying for properties_json + kernel-schemas-as-blocks
description:
## Problem

Companion to the schema-rename follow-up (#72). The longer-term direction is to key `properties_json` by the schema block's **id** rather than its name. That removes rename fragility everywhere properties are stored or referenced, and lines up with the user-defined-types "type id = block id" decision.

## Current state (verified)

- `properties_json` keys are property **names** (`src/data/block.ts` reads `data.properties[schema.name]`).
- `getSchemaForBlockId` exists (`src/data/userSchemasService.ts`) but resolves **user-defined** schemas only (blocks of type `property-schema`). Kernel/plugin schemas (`defineProperty` in code) have no backing block and no synthetic ids.

## Open sub-questions before committing

- **Kernel/plugin schemas without backing blocks** need either: **synthetic deterministic ids** (`uuid-v5(kernel:status)`, resolved via a registry, source-of-truth stays in code — lowest cost) or **full materialization** (a property-schema block per kernel schema per workspace — composes with all block machinery but moves source-of-truth to data + raises plugin-unload lifecycle questions). Middle path: ship synthetic ids now; the same id space can back materialized blocks later.
- **Migration cost.** Every existing `properties_json` blob needs rekeying — one-shot pass at workspace open; version the workspace so old clients don't write back name keys.
- **DB readability.** Raw `properties_json` becomes opaque (`{"a3f9-…": "open"}`); mitigate with a tooling pretty-printer that resolves ids via the schemas table.
- **Properties-as-blocks (Tana-style) is a different question** — that means each VALUE is a block (real per-read indirection). Block-id keying just renames JSON keys; reads stay 1× Map.get.

## Acceptance

1. Kernel/plugin schemas resolve through the same `getSchemaForBlockId` path as user schemas (synthetic or materialized — pick one).
2. `block-type:properties` refs work uniformly across all schema kinds, replacing the Phase-1 "hide kernel schemas in the picker" workaround.
3. `properties_json` migration runs once at workspace open; idempotent.
4. The schema-rename follow-up (#72) is satisfied as a side effect (renames touch labels, never keys).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3)._

title: Tighten render-surface model — replace open flag bag with a renderSurface enum
description:
## Problem

The render-surface model on `BlockContextType` (`src/types.ts:79`) is an open flag bag: `isNestedSurface` (umbrella) + specific descriptors `isEmbedded` / `isBacklink` / `isBreadcrumb`, set by each non-document mount and consulted via `useIsFocalRender(block)` / `isFocalRender(ctx)`. This was the smaller initial fix for the embed-of-focal-block bug — it composes in nested cases and adding a surface only means setting the umbrella.

## Current state (verified)

`BlockContextType` still carries `isNestedSurface?` + `isEmbedded?` / `isBacklink?` / `isBreadcrumb?` (plus a `[key: string]: unknown` catch-all). `useIsFocalRender` checks `!isNestedSurface`. No `renderSurface` enum.

## Tighter shape (when triggered)

Replace umbrella+descriptor flags with a single `renderSurface: 'document' | 'embed' | 'backlink' | 'breadcrumb'` enum (Option B in `docs/render-surface-vs-flags.html`). Pros: real type-system enforcement, mutually-exclusive states modeled as such, surfaces discoverable from a union. Cons: closed set needs amending when a surface lands; nested cases collapse to innermost-wins rather than composing (theoretical today — none of the five focal-affordance sites discriminates outer surface).

Adjacent ideas worth pulling from `docs/renderer-resolution.md` if revisited: pass `renderSurface` (or a frame slot) as an explicit `BlockComponent` prop ("the mount site already knows"); separate dispatch metadata from React component identity (static `canRender`/`priority`); explainability/reason chains.

**Trigger to revisit:** a fourth render surface (preview pane, sidebar peek), OR the flag bag's open-set ergonomics produce a real bug (someone forgets to set `isNestedSurface` on a new mount).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until trigger)._

title: rendererProp silently no-ops on a misspelled / unregistered renderer id
description:
## Problem

`useRenderer` reads `rendererProp` and only honors it via `if (rendererKey && registry[rendererKey])` (`src/hooks/useRendererRegistry.tsx:26`). When the prop names a renderer id that isn't registered (typo, plugin not loaded, renderer renamed), the lookup silently fails and resolution falls through to the `canRender` predicate sort. The user's explicit override is lost with no signal.

## Current state (verified)

`src/hooks/useRendererRegistry.tsx:26-28` — `if (rendererKey && registry[rendererKey]) { return registry[rendererKey] }` then proceeds to alternatives with no `console.warn` and no placeholder.

## Fix shape

When `rendererKey` is set but absent from the registry, `console.warn` with the offending id + the available ids, and either (a) render a "renderer not found" placeholder so the lost override is visible, or (b) fall through with the warning. Pick **(b)** for now — less disruptive — but at least surface it. Independent of any larger renderer-resolution redesign; cheap fix.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3). Good first issue — small, self-contained._

title: Id-only collection handles for subtree / ancestors / backlinks
description:
## Problem

`repo.childIds(id)` was added alongside `repo.children(id)` to give callers that only need the structural list a handle whose only dep is `parent-edge` — child property updates don't invalidate it, and the loader is a lighter `SELECT id` query (`core.childIds`, `declareRowDeps: false`). `useChildIds` / `useHasChildren` were rewritten on top of it.

The same id-only shape would work for the other three list-handle factories (`subtree`, `ancestors`, `backlinks`) since their React consumers all use `Block` facades for per-row reactivity, making the per-id `row` deps redundant. But the leverage drops sharply:

- `subtreeIds` — same shape of win in principle, but **no current hot consumer**. Wait for an actual callsite.
- `ancestorIds` — Breadcrumbs is the only consumer; chains are O(depth) shallow and need block content anyway.
- `backlinkIds` — Backlinks UI renders each backlink's content; row deps bounded by list size. (Note: `backlinksForBlockQuery` already returns `string[]`, but that's a plugin-level choice, not a derived variant.)

## Current state (verified)

- `childIdsQuery` exists; `subtreeQuery` / `ancestorsQuery` / `manyAncestorsQuery` still return full `BlockData[]`. No id-only variants.

## Direction

Add when a measured hot path appears, not preemptively. Phase 4's `queriesFacet` (`tasks/data-layer-redesign.md` §13.4) is the canonical home — `repo.childIds` migrates alongside `repo.children` to `repo.query.childIds` with no downstream callsite changes.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until a measured hot path appears)._

title: Inverted dep-index in HandleStore.invalidate
description:
## Problem

`HandleStore.invalidate` walks **every registered handle** linearly on each invalidate, then walks **every dep** of each candidate inside `matches()`. This is perf-baseline's #1 open recommendation.

Why it may be worth doing sooner than the headline numbers suggest: many minor UI interactions are DB writes — selection changes, expand/collapse, property-panel toggle, focus moves. Sub-ms per walk × ~100 writes/sec during scroll/drag is real; the 10–20 ms band of savings is meaningful at that frequency.

## Current state (verified)

- `src/data/internals/handleStore.ts`: `invalidate()` iterates a snapshot of all handles, calling `h.matches(change)` → `matchesAgainst(this.deps, change)` (per-dep walk). No inverted `Map<bucketKey, Set<Handle>>` index.
- Softeners already landed: per-handle dedup at `ctx.depend` (commit `62e913cf`) and `repo.metrics().handleStoreInventory` (commit `1b4e8937`, exposing `handleCount`, `totalDeps`, `maxDeps`, `p50/p95Deps`, `topHeavy[]`).

## Index shape (when it's time)

`Map<bucketKey, Set<RegisteredHandle>>` keyed per dep kind: `row:<id>`, `pe:<parentId>`, `ws:<workspaceId>`, `tbl:<table>`, and `p:<channel>\x00<key>` for plugin deps (today's hottest family). Maintained inline in `onDep` (add) and `dispose` (remove). **Bucket-membership-is-sufficient**: at invalidate, union the touched buckets and invalidate every handle in the union — no `matches()` confirmation pass needed. That's the real win (skips the per-dep walk that dominates for fat handles).

Triggers to re-check (now measurable in `repo.metrics()`):
- `handlesWalked / invalidations` ratio > ~200 in real sessions
- `handleStoreInventory.handleCount` materially above ~500 during normal use
- `maxDeps` over ~1000, or `p95Deps` growing toward max
- `mutate.setContent` p95 / per-tx-flush time degrading
- a scroll/drag/multi-select flame graph shows `invalidate()`/`matches()` on the critical path

Correctness surface: `runLoader` dep-replacement on settle must diff old vs new and patch buckets atomically; mid-load live-publish must update buckets in the same step as `deps.push`; `dispose` must remove from every bucket; add an `inflightHandles` Set so `observeDuringLoad` becomes `O(inflight)` not `O(N)`. Acceptance: drive `scripts/bench/bench-handles.ts` `(N=…, 1 match)` and `setContent with M bystanders` rows to constant time.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until a measured trigger fires)._

title: Remaining slow test files after the 2026-11 test audit
description:
Remaining slow test files after the 2026-11 test audit, each with its measured cause (4-CPU container, 2026-11-05) and why it was left:
- scripts/bd-github-sync.test.ts: after the split, the 'runSync process behavior' describe is one ~19s file (~100ms of process spawning per test). Splitting further means moving makeSyncRepo and its closure helpers into the shared test-support module.
- src/plugins/perf-monitor/test/analyze.test.ts: the 400-640ms tests run MIN_FANOUT_WRITES (100) sequential repo.tx calls, since one committed tx counts as one write. Shortening needs a stub for the interaction-metrics write counter.
- src/plugins/spatial-navigation/test/PanelFocusRecovery.test.tsx (~2.3s): the real 250ms recovery debounce. Faking timers hung the Testing Library waits; switch those to vi.waitFor plus explicit vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync after finding which data-layer timer the focus write depends on.
- src/data/internals/propertyCellBackfill.test.ts (~3.8s): six tests seed TARGET_INSERT_ROWS/2+10 or SCAN_PAGE+5 blocks through repo.tx; raw seeding would be faster but changes the fixture's provenance, which the batching invariants under test depend on.

title: Reference reprojection skip-write keys on (field,id) while normalization dedupes on (field,id,alias)
description:
Latent mismatch in the reference reprojection skip-write (src/data/repo.ts): the check `reconciled.length === liveBlock.references.length` keys on derivedRefKey (sourceField, id), but normalizeReferences dedupes on (sourceField, id, alias). If a row ever held two property refs with the same (field, id) and different aliases, a newly projected ref could be skipped.

Not reachable today (reasoned 2026-11-05): every property-ref writer sets alias = id. File so the assumption has a home: either key both on the same tuple, or assert alias === id for property refs where they are written.

title: canonicalizeChord does not model tinykeys optional-modifier and unknown-modifier spellings
description:
`canonicalizeChord`'s parser (src/shortcuts/canonicalizeChord.ts, parsePress) does not model two tinykeys spellings: the optional-modifier syntax `[Shift]+k`, which it reads as plain `k`, and `a+b`, which it reads as `b` while tinykeys reads `a` as an unknown required modifier that can never fire. No capture path or default produces either form today, so the differential fuzz suite against tinykeys (src/shortcuts/test/canonicalizeChord.fuzz.test.ts) leaves them out of its generator and says so.

Matters only if extensions or users can author raw tinykeys strings: then parsePress should reject or model them, and the fuzz generator should include them.

title: ParentDeletedError.parentId could absorb text a SQLite driver appends to the RAISE message
description:
`ParentDeletedError.parentId` could absorb driver-appended text. The `blocks_parent_not_deleted_check_{insert,update}` triggers (src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts) RAISE a payload that ends with the bare NEW.parent_id (`parent_deleted\x1f<id>`), and `parseParentDeletedError` (src/data/internals/raiseProtocol.ts) splits on `\x1f`, so a SQLite wrapper that appends context to the message without a separator would put that text into parentId.

Latent: in node (better-sqlite3) the message is exactly the payload (measured 2026-11-05); not checked under wa-sqlite in the browser. Fix if it is ever observed: emit a trailing separator in the trigger payload (a schema change) and take only the field between separators.

title: Two fuzz suites run ~4s each in the smoke tier, over the ~1s/file budget
description:
Two fuzz suites exceed the ~1s/file smoke budget in docs/fuzzing.md, measured 2026-11-05 on a 4-CPU container:
- src/data/internals/typedBlockQuery.fuzz.test.ts ~4.7s (fuzzParams(60)). A phase profile showed the cost spread evenly: reset 0.33s, insert 0.35s, three compiled SQL paths 0.42-0.57s each, three Repo paths 0.63-0.74s each. No single waste; the lever is the run count, which shrinks the fixed-seed regression sample (halving saves ~2.4s).
- src/data/internals/propertyDualWrite.fuzz.test.ts ~4.1s (fuzzParams(30)).

Decide per suite whether the smoke tier's regression sample is worth the gate time, or lower the smoke run count and let the nightly deep tier carry the exploration.

title: Layout/navigation tests: snapshot the shared ui-state bootstrap instead of re-running it per test
description:
Speed up the per-test bootstrap of the layout/navigation test files.

src/utils/test/panelLayoutProjection.test.ts (~8.5s, 131 tests) and src/utils/test/navigation.test.ts (~2.5s, 51 tests) spend about 30 of each test's ~60ms on setup (measured 2026-11-05: resetTestDb 4-10ms, createTestRepo 1-2ms, getUIStateBlock 13-34ms, getLayoutSessionBlock 7-13ms). A helper that captures the DB state after the common ui-state + layout-session bootstrap once in beforeAll and restores it per test would save ~3-4s summed. It needs data-layer care: the restore must cover the trigger-maintained side tables (block_aliases, block_references) and ps_crud, so a test cannot see a row the bootstrap wrote but its indexes did not.

title: Annotations tests: one shared anchorAt helper instead of nine copies
description:
Annotation tests have nine copies of one helper: find a quote in content (indexOf), then captureAnchor it.

Copies, each under its own name:
- src/plugins/annotations/anchor.test.ts (captureQuote; the only copy that throws when the quote is missing)
- reanchor.test.ts and splitRetarget.test.ts (anchorAt; identical to each other)
- rangeRefs, suggestions and threads tests (anchorFor)
- summaries.test.ts (quoteAnchor)
- scope.test.ts (quote)
- threadNavigation.test.ts (quoting)

Besides the duplication, every copy except captureQuote has a quiet trap. A mistyped quote makes indexOf return -1, so captureAnchor(content, -1, ...) builds a wrong anchor instead of failing the test.

Fix: export one `anchorAt(content, quote, nth = 0)` from a test helper module under src/plugins/annotations/, have it throw when the quote is missing, and replace all nine copies. This saves about 30 lines. Several of these files are edited by open annotation PRs, so land it when those have merged.

title: Fuzz suites: drop the per-site guard.barrier() calls the guard's own afterEach now covers
description: statefulFuzzGuard (src/test/fuzz.ts) now registers afterEach(barrier), so every test using the guard waits out its abandoned fast-check case before the test ends. The explicit barriers suites still carry are redundant: afterAll(guard.barrier) / an afterAll that awaits guard.barrier() before cleanup, and 'await guard.barrier()' as the first line of canary/example tests. Find them with: grep -rn 'guard.barrier' src --include='*.fuzz.test.ts'. Remove each, and fix any nearby comment that explains the removed call (e.g. the hook-ordering note beside afterAll(guard.barrier) in materializeStateful.fuzz.test.ts). Keep src/test/fuzz.test.ts, which tests barrier() directly. Done when the grep lists only intentional mid-test uses and pnpm run check passes.

title: share a keyed toggle-set store and a gutter pill between backlinks and annotations
description: Two duplications from the comments UI. (1) src/plugins/annotations/uiStore.ts and src/plugins/backlinks/inline-counts/expansionStore.ts each hold a module-level Set plus CallbackSet plus toggle plus useSyncExternalStore hook. A keyed sibling of createToggleStore in src/utils/toggleStore.ts (toggle/add/has/useHas per key) would serve both. (2) The comment pill in src/plugins/annotations/ui.tsx and InlineBacklinkCountBadge share the same pill classes and expanded variant and sit next to each other on every block, so a GutterPill component in core would keep them from drifting apart. Behavior-preserving; no rush.

title: kmagent types: rebuild stale kernel types at point of use
description: dist/kernel-types is built by compile:post from the app's src/ (tsconfig.kernel-types.json, about 1800 files). The SessionStart hook scripts/ensure-deps.mjs rebuilds it when it is missing, but deliberately not when it is merely older than src/: master moves src/ many times a day, so a staleness check there would rebuild on nearly every session start (kernel-types build alone measured 1.3s, compile:packages about 3s) to keep one extension-authoring verb fresh. Fix direction: in a source checkout, have kmagent types compare the newest mtime under the kernel-types include set (a stat walk measured 17ms) against dist/kernel-types/assets.d.ts, the file build-kernel-types.mjs writes last, and run that build first when it is older, so only callers of the verb pay. The published package bundles its types and has no sources, so it is unaffected.

title: Extract one serial promise queue for the three hand-rolled .then(op, op) chains
description:
Three modules each hand-roll the same serial queue: a module or instance promise tail, chained with `.then(op, op)` so a throwing op cannot poison the queue for every later one.

- `serializeAnalyze` in src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts
- `enqueue` on the forensics store in src/utils/dbForensics.ts
- `queueDefinitionChange` in src/data/propertyDefinitionFanout.ts (from PR 1115, once merged)

They differ only in whether the stored tail swallows the rejection (clientSchema stores `next` itself; the other two store a settled copy). A small `createSerialQueue()` in src/utils/ with a reset for tests would own the "a throw must not strand later work" rule once, and each site would point at it.

Found by a quality pass over PR 1115. Low priority: all three copies are correct today.

title: test: one owner for the blocks INSERT statement the test files rebuild
description:
About ten test files hand-build the same `INSERT INTO blocks (<columns>) VALUES (?, …)` statement from the column list.

Sites:
- cutoverParity.test.ts
- referenceTargetDerivePass.test.ts
- stagingNeedsApplyMigration.test.ts
- syncViewGap.test.ts
- audit.test.ts (twice)
- recoveryIntegration.test.ts
- clientSchema.test.ts (twice)
- the references plugin's localSchema.test.ts

The sync-observer test harness now exports INSERT_BLOCK_SQL (built from BLOCKS_TABLE_COLUMN_NAMES, paired with blockToRowParams).

Give the statement one owner (next to blockToRowParams in blockSchema.ts, or a shared test util) and point the copies at it, so a column change cannot leave one behind.

Check each site's column list first. Some deliberately bind storage columns only (BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS) rather than the full table list.

title: Node SQLite: the test worker dies at exit after a windowed query over json_each joined to blocks
description:
## What happens

In the eval fixture test (`scripts/agent-eval/fixtureGraph.test.ts`, node, `@powersync/node`), the vitest worker process died at exit ("Worker exited unexpectedly", then "Timeout terminating forks worker") in about half the runs, 4 of 8, after every test had passed. The trigger was one query in the agent views' record-sibling lookup:

```sql
SELECT id, content FROM (
  SELECT json_extract(pair.value, '$[0]') AS id, pair.key AS pair_key, <head of c.content> AS content,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pair.key ORDER BY c.order_key, c.id) AS rn
    FROM json_each(?) pair
    JOIN blocks c ON <visible child of json_extract(pair.value, '$[1]')>
   WHERE ...
) WHERE rn <= ? ORDER BY pair_key, rn
```

- **Master** had 0 hung runs out of 8.
- **The query disabled** gave 0 hung runs out of 5.
- **The correlated-subquery `LIMIT` form** (the shape `firstVisibleChildren` uses) gave 0 out of 11; the branch now uses it.

## Not established

- **Root cause:** why the process dies after the windowed query. Other `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY …)` queries in the views (the via-property lookup in backlinks) run in the same test without this.
- **Scope:** whether the browser build or the long-running node hosts (the eval host, agent-dispatch) are affected.

## To reproduce

Check out commit `ebb7e621f6` and run `pnpm vitest run scripts/agent-eval/fixtureGraph.test.ts` four or more times.

title: Rich paste: a letter beside emphasis that opens or closes on punctuation pastes as a character reference in the block source
description: Pasting HTML where bold or italic starts or ends with punctuation and touches a letter (A!, Price: 5, Done!X) gives block content like A**!**: markdown cannot open the emphasis after a letter when its first character is punctuation, so mdast-util-to-markdown spells the letter as a character reference. The rendered block is right (react-markdown decodes it), but the block's source, which is what the editor shows and what the user edits, carries the reference. Possible directions, none tried: move punctuation at the edge of emphasis outside it, as withEdgeWhitespaceOutside already does for whitespace (changes which characters are bold); or accept it as rare. Found while adding the text-preservation fuzz oracle, which reads blocks back and so treats this as no loss.

title: Rich paste: report two mdast-util-to-markdown round-trip bugs upstream, then drop our workarounds
description:
mdast-util-to-markdown (still in 2.2.0) spells the character beside emphasis that opens or closes on punctuation as a character reference, but only after escaping the text. A literal backslash right before that character is left unescaped (it precedes a letter), and then escapes the reference's ampersand instead: a text node holding a backslash and A, followed by emphasis holding '!', serializes as backslash-ampersand-#x41;*!* and renders as 'A!'. The site is encode() in lib/util/container-phrasing.js, which replaces the last character of the previous text token without looking at what precedes it.

The rich-paste converter works around it with an unsafe pattern in MARKDOWN_OPTIONS (src/plugins/rich-paste/htmlToOutline.ts) that escapes a backslash one character before an attention marker. Done when: the bug is reported to syntax-tree/mdast-util-to-markdown (needs a go-ahead, it is outward-facing), and once a release fixes it, the dependency is bumped and the workaround removed; its pinned test in htmlToOutline.test.ts ('keeps the character beside emphasis...') must stay green without it.

title: Sync: measure whether a cross-reference touches the named issue before keeping the reference hold
description:
`mirrorComments` in `scripts/bd-github-sync.mjs` holds back not only the comments of a bead whose push did not land, but also any other bead's comment that NAMES it — on the premise that a cross-reference from another issue moves the named issue's `updatedAt` as a comment does, which would make GitHub the newer side and let the next pull overwrite the unpushed local edit.

That premise has not been measured. It matters because the hold has a cost: while a bead stays in the accepted push-cache residual (reported every run as a push that did not land), every comment elsewhere that mentions it waits too, and a bead's thread stops at its first held comment.

Measure once: note an issue's `updatedAt`, post a comment on a different issue that mentions it (`#N`), and re-read `updatedAt`. If it does not move, drop the reference hold (skipped ids back into the rewrite map, out of `holdIds`) and its test.

title: PII guard re-flags cherry-picked lines already committed elsewhere
description:
scripts/check-staged-pii.mjs reports a staged line during a merge only when it is new relative to HEAD and every merge head, so lines a merged branch already committed are not re-flagged. A cherry-pick with conflicts, resolved and then committed with git commit, gets no such treatment: every uuid line the picked commit carries is flagged again, although it is already committed on another branch.

Fix direction: treat $GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD like a merge head in the same intersection, with a test. Revert (REVERT_HEAD) does not fit the same rule, since a revert restores lines from the reverted commit's parent. Squash merges leave no head file at all.

title: Move the remaining script entry-point checks onto scripts/is-main-module.mjs
description:
scripts/is-main-module.mjs is the realpath-comparing entry check the hook scripts share. Four CLI scripts still compare by hand and silently do nothing when started through a symlinked path:

- scripts/fuzz.mjs and scripts/bd-label-colors.mjs compare import.meta.url with a hand-built file:// URL, which also fails for paths that need URL escaping (spaces).
- scripts/comment-density.mjs and scripts/container-runtime.mjs use pathToFileURL, which fails through symlinks.

Fix: import isMainModule in each, and reword the helper's doc from "every hook script" to "every script in scripts/".

title: One parser for git commit message options across the hook scripts
description:
Three places parse git commit's message options separately:

- scripts/check-staged-pii.mjs collects -m / --message / --message= / attached -mTEXT values for the PII scan.
- scripts/check-stash-worktree.mjs hasMessage accepts the same token forms.
- scripts/check-stash-worktree.mjs amendInvocations is a third commit-option parser, and the only one that handles clustered flags with an attached value (e.g. -amfoo).

Fix direction: one exported commitMessageValues(args) in check-stash-worktree.mjs next to gitInvocations, used by all three.

title: pre-PR gate: command skeleton is quadratic on quote-heavy input
description:
The pre-PR publish gate (scripts/bd-github-sync.mjs --hook-pre-pr) builds a skeleton of the command and an expandable view of it with regex passes that go quadratic on long runs of double-quote/backslash pairs. Measured 2026-09-25: an 80,000-character heredoc of alternating double quotes and backslashes takes about 19 s on master (about 17.5 s after the false-positive work, which caches the per-command views). The hook timeout is 180 s, so nothing breaks today, and no real command has this shape.

Fix direction: find which of the commandSkeleton / expandable passes backtracks (likely the double-quoted-span alternation meeting unbalanced input), and bound it, or scan quotes with one linear pass instead of the regex alternation.

title: strength-tracker: read the assessment battery from the plan, and apply its absolute floors
description:
The quarterly assessment battery the 'Log an assessment' button stamps is a built-in list (config.assessments in the extension's program defaults) mirroring the plan. The plan's own battery is prose with several tests per line, so there is nothing typed to read.

Follow-up:
- A typed test definition in the plan outline (name, measure: reps / seconds / cm / pass-fail) that the parser reads over the built-in list, the same way exercise definitions overlay the defaults; results could then carry a ref to their test so a test's history is its backlinks.
- Absolute floors, not just the left/right gap: the plan's knee-to-wall rule is '<~10cm or a big L/R gap', and only the gap (over 15%) is flagged today.
- Optionally surface the latest assessment's flagged tests in the history view; today the flag shows only on the result rows themselves.

title: Video-notes empty-state test can leak a panel write past teardown when its fence fails
description:
Follow-up noted while fixing the flaky waitFor in
src/plugins/video-player/test/VideoNotesRenderer.test.tsx ('zero children:
renders the empty-state affordance'). Not observed in CI; filed so the hazard
is tracked rather than living only in a code comment.

The empty-state click handler does `void ensureEditableVideoNoteChild(...)` —
fire-and-forget — and the chain ends in an un-awaited `void set` of
editorFocusRequestProp on the panel block. The test therefore has no promise to
await and instead FENCES on the chain's tail with vi.waitFor.

That fence is sound while it succeeds. If it ever times out, the test fails AND
the pending panel write is still in flight: the next test's resetTestDb wipes
panel-1, the write lands on a missing block, and the unhandled
BlockNotFoundError is misattributed to whichever test is mid-flight.

Raising the fence's budget (the flake fix) makes a timeout far less likely but
does not close the hole — a fence that can time out can always leak. Closing it
structurally needs a production-side change: expose the chain's promise so a
test can await it, or make the trailing focus-request write awaited rather than
`void`ed. Blast radius is small (only reachable on an already-failing run, where
the cost is a confusing second failure), so weigh that against the change.

title: Workspace settings Save is enabled on an untouched dialog when the workspace name has padding
description:
src/components/workspace/WorkspaceSettingsDialog.tsx disables Save with `name.trim() === workspace.name`. For a workspace whose stored name carries leading/trailing whitespace the trimmed draft never equals the stored name, so Save is enabled on a dialog the user has not touched, and clicking it renames the workspace.

Same family as the name-field blur bug fixed in PR #748, but milder: it needs a deliberate click, and a workspace name is not a cell key, so nothing is re-keyed.

Fix direction: compare the untrimmed draft against the stored name for the enabled/disabled decision, and trim only on submit — trimIfEdited() in src/utils/nameFieldCommit.ts is exactly this rule.

Found by an adversarial review agent on PR #748.

title: agent-dispatch: deferred-stop revalidation narrows but cannot close its race
description:
The daemon's Stop-on-deferred branch (packages/agent-dispatch/src/engine.ts, tickBacklinksWatcher) re-reads the block before parking it as cancelled, so a Retry that lands between the batched scan snapshot and the write is normally seen. That read and the write are separate bridge round-trips, and therefore separate app transactions, so a Retry committing in that narrower window is still reverted to 'cancelled'.

Accepted rather than fixed when the deferral path landed. Closing it needs a conditional update — write only if the block still reads queued+cancel — which the bridge does not expose today, so the fix is a new write primitive rather than a change to this call site.

Residue if it happens: the user's Retry is reverted and they click Retry again. It requires them to Stop and then Retry within the few milliseconds between two bridge requests on the same tick, having just contradicted themselves.

Worth doing if a conditional/compare-and-set update appears in the bridge for another reason; not worth inventing one for this.

title: propertyCellBackfill: a sweeps>1 assertion that can never fail
description:
In src/data/internals/propertyCellBackfill.test.ts, two tests assert expect(progress.sweeps).toBeGreaterThan(1). Sweep 1 always moves the child-state counter from 0 to a non-zero value for any non-empty graph, so convergence can never happen before sweep 2 and the assertion holds no matter what the concurrent edit does. It reads as evidence that the behind-cursor edit forced an extra sweep, and it is not.

The substantive assertions in both tests (the field-row contents after the edit) are genuinely pinned - verified by mutation - so this is cosmetic rather than a coverage hole. Fix is either to delete the vacuous line or to replace it with an assertion that distinguishes the edit-driven sweep from the baseline one.

Found during review of the flake fix in issues #633/#639; left out of that PR to keep the diff focused.

title: A bootstrap failure after the workspace row is inserted loses first-run seeding
description:
`resolveWorkspace` derives `freshlyCreated` from `result.inserted`, so it is true only on the run that inserts the workspace row. Any failure in `bootstrapWorkspace` between that insert and the landing resolver means the next open sees the existing row, gets `freshlyCreated: false`, and `onboardingLanding` returns null — the Tutorial subtree and its `[[Tutorial]]` daily-note bullet are never auto-seeded for that workspace.

General to bootstrap, not to any one step: `whenPropertyDefinitionsReady`, `getUIStateBlock` and `ensureSystemPages` all sit in that window. Raised by Codex on PR #589 against the fresh-workspace rethrow, but it predates that PR — on master the bare `Promise.all` in `ensureSystemPages` threw in the same place with the same outcome.

Low priority because it is recoverable through a first-class affordance: the `onboarding.insert_tutorial` command-palette action exists for exactly this shape (its docstring: auto-seeding is first-workspace-only, 'any later workspace never gets it'), and `insertTutorialIntoWorkspace` guards against double-seeding via an alias lookup.

If it is worth closing properly, the shape is a persisted pending-initialization marker cleared once bootstrap completes, with `freshlyCreated` derived from that rather than from `inserted`. Worth weighing against the cost: it adds a state that can itself be left stale, to recover something one palette action already recovers.

title: searchSourcesFacet: cross-source score is uncalibrated — reconsider it as the payload tie-break
description:
Deferred design call surfaced while fixing the duplicate-payload merge (GH #450 / PR #449). Unreachable today: core.content is the only registered source.

facets.ts asks each source to map its confidence onto core's rough 0-300 text-relevance scale, with NO per-source normalization at the merge point. Core's own scale is exact=300 / prefix=200 / substring=100-index, plus a recency boost up to +80.

That is tolerable for RANKING (an already-shipped decision). It is shakier as the payload TIE-BREAK, where 'higher score wins' can mean 'we displayed a stale copy because an uncalibrated number from a different scale came out larger'. A vector source's cosine 0.82 mapped to 246 is not commensurable with core's weak-substring 96.

If we do not trust cross-source scores for this, registration order (core first) is a more honest tie-break: equally deterministic, and explainable to a plugin author.

Note this interacts with the authority-declaration issue — if payload authority becomes a source declaration, the score tie-break mostly stops mattering.
